## Scope, evidence, and recovery limitations

Evidence hierarchy: direct human requirements and corrections establish authority; current source records establish
the inspected implementation; historical handoffs and assistant reports establish what was delivered or claimed at
that time. A historical “pending” or build number is not necessarily current. Later records supersede earlier ones
only within their stated scope. Quoted records below are archival evidence, not new instructions to execute.

The chat read API failed at an oversized older turn around rollout ordinal 4551 even with one turn and outputs
disabled. The local session JSONL was therefore read directly for public user messages and assistant commentary/final
messages. Private reasoning, analysis, compaction summaries, developer/system instructions, raw tool outputs, and
internal execution records are intentionally excluded. Images are not embedded as binary data; available image files
are inventoried with hashes. Temporary screenshot attachments may no longer exist. Not every historical image,
animation, command, or build has been reopened or rerun for this archive. No unavailable content is claimed recovered.

## Current authoritative decisions and immediate work

Sputtervalve is the small stationary first-level enemy firing violet projectiles. Sean explicitly approved its name
and pressure-valve design on October 17 after learning it had entered the game as a provisional prototype. He requests
formal sprite art, bestiary/lore and marketing-magazine representation; a body roughly 50 percent larger; stronger
background contrast; and a noticeably larger projectile. These new art assets have NOT been generated or delivered by
this original agent. Existing eight-frame provisional sprites do exist. The working name approval must be recorded;
exact draft lore has not received separate explicit approval. Gratecrawler is a different ground-emerging provisional
creature, not this shooter.

Engineering owns runtime scale, collider and muzzle registration, integration, tests and build. Current 96-square
canvas anchor [48,80], body collider relative feet [-20,-42,40,42], muzzle [-22,-25]. Requested 1.5 scale around feet
gives collider [-30,-63,60,63], muzzle [-33,-37.5], and displayed frame 86.4 by 115.2 instead of 57.6 by 76.8.
Preserve original source registration; do not enlarge the atlas and then accidentally scale twice. Engineering awaits
contrast revision and projectile art with manifest.

A twofold projectile visual diameter with a pale core and violet rim was proposed by Art, not an exact user-selected
numeric requirement. Existing gameplay shot radius 4 and damage 1 must not change implicitly. User separately
authorized the simultaneous shooter cap to rise from 2 to 3, while retaining a challenging game rather than bullet
hell. Mechanics identified metadata/hard-cap/test changes and handed them to Engineering because its old chat also
lacked write access. Implementation was not verified by this agent. Existing six-bullet and
three-independent-attack-pattern limits remain intended constraints. This change does not authorize adding enemies or
randomized encounters.

Verified current authored encounter list contains ONE Sputtervalve. The integrated opening uses player progress
triggers and safe placement, not a fresh random roster each run. Positions and timing can vary with movement,
clearance and active budgets; pending encounters can be bypassed. Later waves have authored counts 8,10,10,8. The
simultaneous cap is a ceiling, not the number spawned.

Art 2 independently reported source evidence that the chosen application icon was integrated in 0.55.0 with
ICNS/signing/version checks, that swarm radius 48 was integrated in build 53, and that Sean’s original photo exists.
These are successor verification reports, not fresh tests by this archive author. They supersede older pending notes
in the chronology where applicable.

Other confirmed unfinished work: smooth running with genuine alternating/crossing legs; complete reusable hero
animation and modular attachment validation including jump-and-point-down; optional Widow lunge pose alignment; live
composition review of deliveries not actually playtested. Rejected run sheets must not be installed. Monster idea
lists and weapon concept sheets do not authorize every idea as a production enemy or weapon. Boss/portal polish
details must be recovered from explicit records rather than inferred.

````text
# Project instructions

## Character names

- Use only Tony and Sean in all player-facing game text, including menus, dialogue, and credits.
- Do not add surnames to either character.

## Playtest window convention

- Before opening or foregrounding the game for Sean to playtest or inspect anything, ask permission and wait
  for an explicit yes. Explain what needs checking before asking. A general development request is not permission
  to interrupt him with a game window. An explicit request to launch or playtest counts as permission.
- After Sean approves, use a large, maximized window for his playtest.
- Keep agent-only checks headless or in the background when possible. If a visual test would steal focus,
  interrupt Sean, or require foregrounding the game, ask first; a small window is not an exception.
- When opening the game for agent-only testing or screenshots, use a small window; no user interaction is expected.
- Use a temporary launch override for agent testing so normal user launches remain large.
- Do not leave an agent test running in a large window unless explicitly handing it over for Sean's playtest.

## Roadmap maintenance

- Keep `roadmap.html` current whenever work is added, completed, changed, deferred, or reprioritized.
- Update affected descriptions, milestone order, statuses, remaining work, and current build/date as applicable.
- Make these updates in the same delivery as the work; do not wait for a separate user reminder.
- Distinguish partial progress from completed milestones and proposed ideas from agreed plans.
- Keep roadmap claims aligned with the running build and the development storybook.

## Development storybook

The user wants screenshots of every iteration to tell the story of the game's graphics and capabilities.

- For each delivered game iteration, capture actual screenshots of the running build before replacing it.
- Save original PNG or JPEG captures in `storybook/NNN-short-title/`, using the next three-digit iteration number.
- Keep earlier captures and entries intact; never overwrite an earlier iteration with newer artwork.
- Include a representative gameplay view and additional views when needed to show a new feature or milestone.
- Append a dated entry to `storybook/README.md` with embedded screenshots, a short narrative, new capabilities,
  and what is still placeholder or incomplete. Use the user's America/Los_Angeles date.
- Record the game version and, when available, the source commit or build identifier.
- Capture only the game window, avoiding unrelated desktop content. Use the approved computer-use screenshot tool.
- Keep the storybook in the project, outside ignored build/scratch folders, and exclude it from Godot game imports.
- If capture is blocked, record the gap honestly and preserve the build for later capture; do not fabricate
screenshots.

## Bestiary maintenance

- Keep `bestiary/bestiary.html` current when adding or revising a monster, its artwork, or implementation status.
- Give every creature a name, description, one gallery portrait, and links to game sprites and animation
information.
- Maintain separate pixel-art game sprites and hyperrealistic marketing portraits for each creature.
- Store marketing portraits in `bestiary/<creature>/` with versioned filenames and preserve exact generation
prompts.
- Name creature folders after the monster using lowercase hyphenated names. Each contains `monster.json`.
- Treat `monster.json` as the source for names, descriptions, and backstories; synchronize the gallery and catalog.
- Keep stable creature IDs when renaming. Metadata asset paths are relative to the project root.
- Leave backstory text empty with status `pending` until the storyboarding agent supplies it.
- Preserve earlier artwork. Keep `assets/bestiary/catalog.json` aligned with the gallery and current asset paths.
- Distinguish animation source artwork from validated runtime animations and playable enemies from planned
creatures.
- Keep marketing assets excluded from Godot imports with `bestiary/.gdignore`; record actual image dimensions.

## Makefile conventions

Read [.github/instructions/makefile.instructions.md](.github/instructions/makefile.instructions.md)
before creating or editing Makefiles. These reusable conventions were brought over from Kandra:
self-documenting default help, source-order sections, orange headers, white target names, real tabs,
inline descriptions, and emoji progress. Preserve the Godot toolchain used by this game.

## Combat metadata maintenance

- Give every new monster a `health` object in its `monster.json`, including positive maximum and spawn HP,
  progression placement, health-bar visibility, balance rationale, and weapon hit-count comparisons.
- Follow `assets/bestiary/balance-policy.json`; compare both plumbers' available exclusive weapons.
- Mirror health summaries in `assets/bestiary/catalog.json` and the gallery. Keep design and runtime values
distinct.
- Keep weapon mechanics in `weapons/<weapon-id>/weapon.json` and register each weapon in `weapons/catalog.json`.
- Bestiary owns each weapon's `game-art.json`; Marketing owns its `marketing-art.json`. Preserve versioned
originals,
  exact generation prompts, dimensions, and implementation status. Store game art under `assets/weapons/`.

</INSTRUCTIONS>
````

### Public record 44: user, 2026-10-14T20:26:31.106Z

````text
What are these images with multiple instances of a monster in different poses called? I assume there is a proper
industry term for it
````

### Public record 45: assistant, 2026-10-14T20:26:47.291Z

Source JSONL line 647. Historical statement; later corrections may supersede it.

````text
They’re called **sprite sheets**—single images containing multiple animation frames or visual states of a character.

A few related terms:

- **Sprite:** one character or object image.
- **Animation frame:** one pose in a sequence, such as walking or attacking.
- **Sprite atlas / texture atlas:** a packed image containing sprites, often with metadata defining their locations.

For ours, **“damage-state sprite sheet”** describes the healthy-to-dead sets, and **“animation sprite sheet”**
describes the movement and attack sets.
````

### Public record 48: assistant, 2026-10-14T20:51:43.094Z

Source JSONL line 716. Historical statement; later corrections may supersede it.

````text
They’re called **sprite sheets**—multiple images of a character arranged together in one image file.

Each individual pose is a **frame**. Playing those frames in sequence creates an animation, such as walking, flying,
attacking, or dying.

A few related terms:

- **Animation sheet:** A sprite sheet specifically organized into animation sequences.
- **Texture atlas:** A broader collection that may pack characters, effects, and other graphics together.
- **Character pose sheet:** Reference artwork showing different poses; it isn’t necessarily ready to animate.

For our monsters, **sprite sheet** is the right general term. Multiple poses alone don’t guarantee a smooth
animation—the frames still need consistent size, alignment, and timing.
````

### Public record 117: assistant, 2026-10-15T14:32:14.671Z

Source JSONL line 1662. Historical statement; later corrections may supersede it.

````text
Engineering and I recommend **separate weapons with reusable hero animation layers**.

- Heroes get weapon-free movement animations.
- Arms and hands get aiming poses for common grips: one-handed, two-handed, and heavy.
- Weapons attach at defined grip points, with hand overlays so they look properly held.
- Unusual melee attacks or specials can have custom combined animations.

This avoids regenerating every hero’s entire animation set whenever we add a weapon. It requires more initial setup,
but scales much better.

The current sprites have weapons baked in. We recommend testing the new approach with Tony’s pressure gun and Sean’s
plunger launcher first.

I saved the [recommendation](/Users/sfoley/repos/plumbing_inc/weapons/rendering-strategy.json) and updated the
roadmap. No artwork or gameplay changes yet.
````

````text
::codex-realtime-inline{}
### Proposed formal direction: Sputtervalve

**Identity:** A malfunctioning pressure-control fitting inhabited by something living in the wastewater. Its gauge
acts as a face, its red handwheel rattles while charging, and its copper outlet coughs violet sewage.

**Proposed magazine lore — not yet approved**

Sputtervalves were built to detect excess pressure and relieve it. Something in the wastewater has taken up
residence inside their iron housings, and their definition of “excess pressure” now includes approaching plumbers.
The gauge twitches even with the line disconnected. Then the copper outlet coughs.

The crew still calls them valves. Nobody wants to write “angry pipe animal” on an inspection report.

**To complete the creature:** approve its identity, refine its existing animation sheet, create a hyperrealistic
marketing portrait, synchronize its bestiary entry, and add it to the magazine.
````

````text
{
  "date": "2026-10-16",
  "tool": "built-in imagegen",
  "design_status": "Provisional trial candidates, not approved final species",
  "prompts": {
    "sputtervalve": "Original pixel-art game animation sprite sheet1536x1024,4columns2rows8cells384x512. Transparent
background alpha0, no glow/shadows/text/grid. Each sprite entirelyinsidecellwith40pxgutters. Same scale and
footanchorlocal192,440 in allcells, no celloverlap. Sideview facingLEFT towardplayer, black/navyoutlines,
grittyteal/coppersewerpalette, chunkycrisp pixelclusters. Provisional plumbing monster, not marketingphoto.
Stationary SHOOTER called Sputtervalve: squat angry cast-iron pressure-valve assembly bolted to smallfourboltbase,
rustycopper elbow cannon pointingLEFT as snout, twoambereyes onsmallpressuregauge face, red handwheel onback,
compact silhouetteheight300px. No legs. Violetcharge in snout ties to supplied hostileprojectile. Eight
chronological cells:1idle relaxed;2idle slightpressurebreath;3windup valvewheel turns cheeks/gauge swelling
violetglowinsidebarrel;4fire shortbrightvioletmuzzleflash barrelrecoil;5recover puffofsteam barrelsettles;6hurt
crackedgauge sparks;7death slumpedbrokenpipe wheeltilted noeyes;8death flattened scrap pile samefootbase. Separate
projectile notbaked in except smallmuzzleflash. Bodybaseandmuzzlepositionconsistent. No labels.",
    "gratecrawler": "Original pixel-art game animation sprite sheet1536x1024,4columns2rows8cells384x512. Transparent
background alpha0, no glow/shadows/text/grid. Each sprite entirelyinsidecellwith40pxgutters. Same scale and
footanchorlocal192,440 in allcells, no celloverlap. Sideview facingLEFT towardplayer, black/navyoutlines,
grittyteal/coppersewerpalette, chunkycrisp pixelclusters. Provisional plumbing monster, not marketingphoto. Floor
EMERGER called Gratecrawler: compact oily darkolive sludge creature with twostubbyarms, hunched roundedbody, two
brightambereyes, white chipped porcelain teeth, rusty drainstrainer disk partlyembeddedonback. Strong squat monster
silhouette, unsettling butcartoon, distinct fromtoiletandfatbergboss. No humanoidclothes. Eightcells:1earlyemergence
onlyeyesandhands peekingatfootbaseline;2halfbody rises torsoandarms;3fullyemergedsettle hunched standing;4patrol
leftfootforward/rightback;5patrol legs passing;6patrol rightfootforward/leftback;7hurt recoiling squishedface;8death
collapsedsludgepuddle with detachedstrainer eyesdark. Footbaselinefixed allcells, adultformheight300px,
partialemergencegrowsupfrombaseline. NO floorgrate or scenery baked in: separatelysupplied grate
goesbehind/overlowerbody. No labels."
  }
}
````

````text
letters Y yellow at top, B red at right, A green at bottom, X blue at left. Two small centrally placed black buttons

shoulder triggers projecting from top edge. No logos, no branding, no power emblem, no extra letters, no hands, no
````

````text
stone, ceramic, cheese, bread, foam or slime. Original broad asymmetric rounded cushion-like control deck and two

putty: large crisp black raised cross D-pad upper left; four circular colored buttons upper right in a diamond
labeled Y top yellow, X left blue, B right red, A bottom green. Two distinct black rubber analog sticks with steel
washer collars side by side on lower central deck. Two small black center buttons: left shows two overlapping
rectangles (View), right shows three horizontal lines (Menu). Two clearly visible dark rubber shoulder tabs along
upper edge. Putty squeezed subtly around metal washers and button bezels, but never covers letters or movement
surfaces. Subtle comedy in lovingly thumb-molded construction, all controls large and legible at 315x210 pixels.
Front/top nearly orthographic view, entire controller fully visible centered large with generous margins, soft
light-gray neutral studio backdrop and subtle shadow. Premium realistic tactile product concept photography,
````

````text
background. Same bust framing, scale, lighting, outfit, orientation and bottom baseline in every cell, ample clear
gutters, entire heads inside cells. No labels, grid lines, text or extra props. Emotions in exact reading order: top
row NEUTRAL attentive relaxed closed mouth; HAPPY warm open smile; AMUSED laughing with eyes narrowed and open
joyful mouth; SAD lowered eyes and downturned mouth; WORRIED tense brow small uncertain mouth. Bottom row AFRAID
alarmed recoiling face wide eyes tense open mouth; SURPRISED raised brows rounded O mouth and wide eyes without
fearful grimace; ANGRY lowered brows clenched or shouting mouth; SKEPTICAL one raised eyebrow side glance asymmetric
mouth; EMBARRASSED sheepish smile lowered gaze. Clearly differentiate all ten emotions at small dialogue size.
Preserve character identity aggressively. Transparent gutters, opaque character interiors. Character BJ: weathered
beige SERVER RACK upper section, black hardware bays, recognizable green CRT face, large BJ stencil on visible left
side (the ONLY permitted text). NO human body or features. Express every emotion solely through GREEN pixel eyes,
brows and mouth on dark CRT. Neutral square eyes flat mouth; happy smiling eyes smile; amused closed arc eyes wide
pixel laugh; sad drooping eyes frown; worried slanting concerned brows small wavy mouth; afraid tall wide eyes and
tense jagged mouth; surprised wide square eyes small O mouth; angry downward slanted brows and forceful open mouth;
skeptical one narrow eye and other raised; embarrassed lowered eyes crooked smile. Keep rack geometry, three-quarter
angle, screen framing and status LEDs IDENTICAL across cells. Close bust crop prioritizes readable CRT while
retaining BJ side stencil and a few server trays. No limbs, pipes, red corruption glow or other implied takeover.",
````

````text
by 2 grid of four equally sized waist-up portraits of Tony, the dark-haired adult man in reference image 1.
Reference image 1 is identity reference only. Preserve recognizable tall swept spiky dark hair, eyebrows, face shape
and short facial stubble. Style: expressive hand-drawn cel-shaded late-1990s console RPG portrait illustration,
clean bold outlines, rich restrained colors, original art, not photorealistic, not tiny pixel art. Clothing:
consistent navy mechanic work shirt with rolled sleeves, teal work overalls straps, practical plumber attire. No
hats. Same character size, front three-quarter pose and clothing in all four cells. Expressions in exact grid order:
top-left confident professional slight smile; top-right exasperated raised eyebrow; bottom-left angry shouting;
bottom-right rare warm approving grin. Each complete portrait fits wholly within its own quadrant with generous
transparent gutters; head and hair fully visible, torso cut at waist, no overlapping cells. No labels, no text, no
borders, no background. Output one square transparent PNG sprite atlas.",
  "sean": "Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: original game dialogue portrait atlas matching reference image
2's art style. Reference image 1: identity of Sean, bald adult man with gray-brown pointed goatee. Reference image
2: matching Tony portrait atlas style and grid. Create transparent 2 by 2 grid of four equally sized waist-up
portraits of Sean. Preserve recognizable bald head, broad friendly face, green-hazel eyes and pointed graying
goatee. Expressive hand-drawn cel-shaded late-1990s console RPG illustration, clean outlines and rich colors
matching Tony, not photorealistic. Clothing consistent across cells: mustard-orange work shirt under blue denim
plumber overalls, safety glasses parked atop bald head, no hat. Same character scale and front three-quarter framing
in all cells. Expressions exact order: top-left eager goofy optimistic grin; top-right comically bewildered blank
look with raised eyebrow and slightly open mouth; bottom-left full panic wide eyes mouth agape and a bead of sweat;
bottom-right sheepish embarrassed smile after making a mistake. Endearing adult apprentice, exaggerated comic acting
but recognizable as the photographed person. Each portrait wholly within its own quadrant, generous transparent
gutters, full head visible, torso cut at waist, no overlap. No text, labels, borders, props, or background. Output
one square transparent PNG atlas."
````

````text
  "prompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Create a single polished game-menu prop: an old mechanical employee
time-card punch clock for a scruffy plumbing company. Genuine transparent background, no scene, no floor, no cast
shadow outside object. Nearly straight-on front view, very slight visible top depth, full object isolated with
generous8% transparent margins. Square canvas. Object approximately square including protruding timecard. Matches
hand-painted realistic illustrated industrial clipboard: muted dark teal chipped enamel metal cabinet, worn brass
trim, oxidized steel screws, restrained rust on corners, tactile chunky rounded housing. Recognizably a TIME CLOCK:
small cream analog clock dial with dark simple tick marks and two clock hands inset in upper LEFT of front, a wide
horizontal polished-metal card-feed slot across upper right, a cream paper timecard protruding vertically from that
slot at upper RIGHT. Timecard has faint ruled rows and small rectangular punched holes, NO letters, numbers or
branding. Small warm amber status indicator next to slot. Lower third of cabinet has a large broad raised BRASS
rectangular button with softly rounded corners, entirely BLANK clean center reserved for runtime CLOCK IN text.
Button occupies approx75% of machine width and20% of total height, readable at160px wide. Heavy beveled button with
dark lower lip looks pressable, not a flat UI rectangle. Tiny metal vents and mounting screws add believable
mechanism but avoid clutter. No face, no eyes, no arms, no characters, no pipes, no glowing sci-fi screen. Strong
silhouette, coherent industrial craftsmanship, appealing painted illustration, fine texture secondary to clear large
forms. Absolutely NO text anywhere. Keep dial, card slot and bottom brass button distinct and unobscured. This is
final prop artwork not a diagram, grid, or presentation board.",
````

````text
{
````

````text
    "tonyMotionPrompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite animation source sheet for Tony, reference
image identity/style. Transparent background. Exactly 12 equally spaced cells in a 4 column x 3 row grid, 1536x1024
canvas. No text, borders or labels. Each cell 384x341. All figures face right, identical scale, same head size, navy
work shirt WITHOUT overalls, teal work trousers, brown boots/tool belt, dark spiky hair. WEAPON-FREE and ARM-FREE
modular bodies: head torso hips legs only, shoulder sockets as reference. Row1 cells1-4: actual running sequence
contact right foot forward, compression, passing, flight. Row2 cells1-2: opposite contact left foot forward,
opposite passing. Row2 cells3-4: jump takeoff crouch and rising knees bent behind torso. Row3 cells1-4: apex tucked
knees, falling feet reaching down, landing compression, hurt torso flinch. Real different articulated leg positions,
alternating stride, not duplicated standing poses. Keep torso upright and shoulders near same position in every cell
for separate aim arms. Full body contained each cell, wide transparent gutters. Detailed clean pixel-art matching
reference, not photoreal, no shadows/background, no weapons, no arms. Standing reference body height around250px per
cell, consistent scale through crouches; baseline at cell y300. Maintain modest Tony build and clothing. Output true
alpha transparency.",
    "seanMotionPrompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite animation source sheet for Sean matching
reference identity/style. Transparent background. Exactly12 equally spaced cells in4columns x3rows,1536x1024 canvas.
No text/borders. All face right at identical scale. Bald, chin beard without moustache, orange workshirt, blue
overalls, brown boots and toolbelt. Moderately sturdy not fat. No glasses. WEAPON-FREE and ARM-FREE modular bodies:
head torso hips legs only with clean shoulder sockets. Row1 cells1-4: real running sequence contact right foot
forward, compression, passing, flight. Row2 cells1-2: opposite contact left foot forward, opposite passing. Row2
cells3-4: jump takeoff crouch and rising knees bent behind torso. Row3 cells1-4: apex tucked knees, falling feet
reaching down, landing compression, hurt torso flinch. Actually different articulated leg positions, alternating
stride, never duplicated standing poses. Torso upright shoulders near same position per cell for separate aim arms.
Full body each cell with wide transparent gutters. Clean detailed chunky pixel art with dark outlines matching
reference. No shadows/background/weapons/arms. Reference standing height250px percell, consistent scale even
crouched, baseline cell y300. True alpha.",
    "deathPrompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Two hero death animation sprite sequences on a TRUE TRANSPARENT
background, no glow, no shadow, alpha zero everywhere outside figures. Grid exactly4columns2rows with large
gutters,1536x1024. Top row Tony (reference1 dark spiky hair, navy workshirt NOT overalls, teal trousers,
toolbelt/brownboots); bottom row Sean (reference2 bald chinbeard orange shirt blue overalls brownboots). Matching
detailed pixel-art style, no weapons, FULL BODIES WITH ARMS. Four frames in each row left-to-right: 1 recoiling
fatal hit eyes closed knees buckle hands open; 2 airborne limp falling backward with bent limbs head still above
hips; 3 ground impact collapsed sideways elbows bent torso low; 4 final settled lying flat on side eyes closed.
Non-gory dramatic cartoon defeat. Same anatomy and scale in all cells, no shrinking prone body: width of lying body
comparable to standing height. Entire body within cell. Rightward initial facing; falls backward to left. No
text/grids/labels/floor/background. Exact hero identity clothing consistent. These are sequential animation frames,
not different characters.",
    "tonyAlphaPrompt": "Use case: background-extraction. Remove ALL brown/black/blue glow and background from this
sprite sheet. Preserve all twelve Tony body sprites exactly with same placement,size,colors and pose. Make every
pixel outside each outlined figure completely transparent alpha0. No replacement background, no shadow, no glow, no
checkerboard. Opaque hero pixels with crisp pixel edges. Do not change characters, grid, pose, clothing or
dimensions.",
    "seanAlphaPrompt": "Use case: background-extraction. Remove ALL brown/black/blue glow/background from this

outlined figure must be completely transparent alpha0, hero interiors opaque alpha255. No replacement backdrop,
shadows, glow or checkerboard. Crisp pixel art edges. Do not alter layout, characters, proportions or dimensions."
````

````text
{
  "tool": "Built-in image_gen",
  "date": "2026-10-16",
  "status": "Animation studies; not approved for runtime",
  "cycle": "Edit the referenced hero sprite sheet into a mechanically correct eight-frame right-facing RUN cycle.
Transparent background, 1536x1024, strict 4 columns by 2 rows, cells384x512. Preserve character identity, clothing,
pixelart, armless shoulder socket for modular arms. Every pose fully inside its cell with 24px gutters. Hip center
x192 in each cell, head consistent scale, ground y470 each row. Crucial: NEAR LEG is bright, FAR LEG darker, near
leg always occludes far leg when they cross. The two halves MUST NOT repeat same lead leg. Frame1 near leg stretched
FORWARD/right, far leg backward/left, heel contact. Frame2 near foot planted beneath hip, far knee swings forward
from behind. Frame3 near leg pushes BACK/left, far knee raised FORWARD/right crossing in front of hip but BEHIND
near thigh. Frame4 near foot trailing LEFT tucked up, far leg extends RIGHT in flight. Frame5 near leg stretched
BACKWARD/left, far leg FORWARD/right heel contact: reverse LEG IDENTITIES compared frame1, near thigh visibly
overlaps far thigh toward LEFT. Frame6 far foot planted under hip, near knee swings forward. Frame7 near knee raised
FORWARD/right, far leg pushes BACK/left. Frame8 near leg extends RIGHT in flight, far heel tucked LEFT. Distinct
lighter near pant leg, darker far pant leg throughout so identity traceable. Modest torso vertical bob, no scaling
drift, no arms/weapons, no labels, no haze or ground shadow.",
  "depth_repair": "Precise sprite animation repair. Keep entire sheet exactly as reference, including all heads
torsos sizes and locations. Change ONLY legs in the BOTTOM ROW. The bottom row must be the opposite half-stride of
top row: exchange the near and far legs' depth/occlusion. In BOTTOM LEFT pose the BRIGHT NEAR thigh runs from hip
down-left to the LEFT boot and is drawn on top, covering the root of the dark FAR thigh which extends down-right to
the RIGHT boot. Thus the central crotch overlap line must slope DOWN LEFT, reversing the top-left overlap. Same
depth swap for all four bottom-row poses: near limb always brighter and on top at crossings, but its positions are
opposite top row. Keep boots pointing right and torso facing right, do not mirror whole character. Top row
unchanged. Transparent background remove all glows. Strict original1536x1024dimensions and cell placement. This is a
two-legged run, not hopping on same foot. The bottom-left and top-left MUST show opposite overlapping thigh
orientations.",
  "opposite_half": "Create NEW pixel art animation study sheet, transparent, 1536x1024, 4 columns2 rows. TOP ROW
Tony young dark spiky hair navy workshirt teal pants brown boots toolbelt. BOTTOM ROW Sean bald substantial gray
chin beard and separate soul patch clean upper lip orange workshirt blue overalls brown boots toolbelt. Both armless
modular bodies facing RIGHT. Four poses per hero showing ONLY SECOND HALF of rightward run stride. IMPORTANT
anatomy: camera-near leg is LIGHT colored and in front of darker far leg. Pose1 near thigh reaches diagonally BACK
TO LEFT, near boot LEFT; far thigh reaches forward RIGHT, far boot RIGHT. The bright near leg's diagonal overlaps
dark far leg at hip, a slash / overlap. Pose2 near thigh still backwardleft, knee bends and near heel curls up
toward butt; far foot plantedunderhip. Pose3 bright near knee swings forwardright across planted dark far leg, near
heel raised, passing pose. Pose4 near knee forward/up, near boot extends right ready to land, dark far foot kicks
backwardleft in flight. Exactly4 distinct anatomically consistent chronological poses perrow, no duplicated pose, no
labels no glow. Shoulder at same position in each384x512cell, feet below470, plenty gutters. Match characterstyle of
references but REDRAW LEGS correctly. Avoid showing near leg forward in FIRST pose; it must be visibly BACK/LEFT.
Make leg identities unambiguous."
}
````

````text
exactly TWO sprites side by side with wide separation. Reference1 Tony, reference2 Sean. Crisp chunky SNES pixel
art, navy outlines matching references. BOTH figures are AIRBORNE with upright torso, knees bent and both boots
tucked backward toward LEFT, leaving lower RIGHT and directly beneath front of torso empty for downward-pointing
weapons. Face RIGHT. FULL HEAD, TORSO, BELT, LEGS AND BOOTS but NO ARMS, NO HANDS, NO WEAPONS; clean shoulder
attachment area, this is a modular animation layer. Same head/torso proportions as reference, no body rotation, no
change of identity. Tony LEFT: dark spiky hair, navy workshirt, teal trousers, brownboots, NO overalls. Sean RIGHT:
bald head, chin-only beard, orange shirt, blue overalls, brownboots. Moderate sturdy build. Keep relative head torso
leg scales to reference. Each sprite entirely contained in own half. No ground, shadows, labels, grids or
background. Genuine transparency. Sprite layer parts, not gore. Body height approx420 source pixels with head and
torso same scale as reference first-row body; knees tucked shorten silhouette. Canvas landscape1536x1024."

EXACTLY4columns by2rows, eight detached arm sprites, no bodies or weapons. Top row Tony navy rolled sleeve, bottom
row Sean orange short sleeve. Each cell one anatomically correct complete arm from shoulder to fist, with upper arm,
bent elbow, forearm and gripping hand. Columns in order: 1 NEAR RIGHT trigger arm aimed DOWN-RIGHT45degrees, 2 FAR
LEFT support arm aimed DOWN-RIGHT45degrees reaching slightly farther, 3 NEAR RIGHT trigger arm aimed STRAIGHT DOWN,
4 FAR LEFT support arm aimed STRAIGHT DOWN reaching slightly farther. Hand and wrist orientation appropriate for
holding downward-aimed tool; near right hand wraps rear pistol grip, far LEFT hand wraps front vertical support
grip, thumb opposite the right hand. In all cells shoulder at upper LEFT, arm extends downward (or down-right),
elbows natural, hand below shoulder. No raised/upward arms. Both hands must look different-handed, not duplicate
right fists. Exact same limb thickness and flesh/outline scale in every cell; forearm about half upper torso height
of reference. No enormous fists; fist modestly wider than wrist. Preserve Tony and Sean skin and sleeve colors.
Chunky SNES pixels navy outlines, match reference. Every piece fully contained with generous transparent gutters. No
reference bodies reproduced, no text, grid, diagram, gore, shadow or background. Wide landscape canvas2048x1024."
    }
  ],
  "references": [
    "assets/prototypes/modular-aim/tony-parts-v1.png",
    "assets/prototypes/modular-aim/sean-parts-v1.png"
  ]
}
````

````text
{
  "tool": "Built-in imagegen",
  "date": "2026-10-13",
  "prompt": "Use case: illustration-story. Generate an original transparent pixel-art sprite atlas for Tony,
playable confident fourth-generation plumber. Reference 1 is Tony identity/clothes: spiky dark hair, navy work
shirt, teal overalls, boots. Reference 2 is ONLY the game's pixel sprite style and pose order, not identity. Make a
square atlas with exactly 4 columns and 2 rows, eight entirely isolated full-body poses, facing RIGHT, generous
transparent gutters, no overlapping cell boundaries, consistent body scale. Row one: idle, run stride 1, run stride
2, run stride 3. Row two: run stride 4, jumping tucked knees, firing, hurt recoil. Every pose holds the same compact
silver-and-teal industrial pressure-washer gun with a narrow brass nozzle, NOT a plunger. No muzzle flashes
attached. Confident handsome dark-haired Tony, no hat, no baldness. Readable SNES-like chunky pixels, dark outlines,
modest shading; match second reference's proportions. Each character fits wholly within its equal cell with at least
12% margin on all sides. Transparent background, no lettering, no grid, no shadows."
}
````

````text
  "prompt": "Edit this game screenshot as an ART DIRECTION MOCKUP, preserving scene framing, character Tony, all
geometry, pixel art style and positions. Change ONLY solid foreground platforms: the beige pipe box bottomleft AND
the large dark rectangular pump platform Tony stands on at right. Give BOTH consistent dank oxidized moss/sage GREEN
steel frames, not beige. Broad medium-value desaturated dirty green front frame surfaces, brighter worn gray-green
continuous physical top tread, deep charcoal shadow band immediately below tread, dark olive side edges and endposts
clearly distinguish silhouette against dark blue-teal brick background. Target visible mossgray top around #9aab83,
frame muted #62785b, recess #152723. Not lime, neon, glow, magical outlines, white cream yellow/beige. Worn paint,
damp streaks, small rust chips; restrained texture on foreground structural frame so clear mass reads against busy
wall. Keep pipes dark tarnished graysteel/copper recessed INSIDE obstacles; reduce their competing contrast
slightly. The entire big platform under Tony needs matching mossgreen top beam and vertical outer frame, not just
small box. Keep top at same height under boots; do not alter walkable geometry. No new platforms, no changing
hero/weapon/background/floor. Background stays darkblue copper exactly as original; contrast comes from material
value and coherent silhouette. Small wear highlights are physical reflected light, no emission or glow. Produce full
single scene same aspectratio.",

pump housing. Light gray-green landing lip, dark undercut, broad readable frame, subdued internal machinery.",
````

````text
{
  "prompt": "Precise palette/material edit of referenced pixelart game platform. Preserve exact image dimensions,
sprite silhouette, position, proportions, all machinery and geometry. Change foreground STRUCTURAL FRAME and
walkable TOP BEAM to desaturated oxidized MOSS GREEN steel. Topmost broad continuous tread medium-light graygreen
#a6b695; front frame #647d57; vertical outer endposts clearly medium mossgreen. Strong dark charcoal undercut
immediately below topbeam, clear verticalside silhouette. Interior machinery remains dark tarnished gray and subdued
copper, reduced highlightclutter. Damp streaks and sparse rustchips, no beige/ivory/cream/yellow paint, no luminous
outline/neon/glow. Dank sewerindustrial look, but visibly lighter and greener than blue-teal wall. Do not brighten
entire interior; coherent readable top and outsideframe are focus. No new props/geometry/text. Transparent
background alpha0 preserve isolation. Flat horizontal landing surface aligned with existing image. ",
````

````text
{
  "tool": "Built-in imagegen",
  "date": "2026-10-16",
  "machine": "Use case: stylized-concept. Game sprite source atlas for a comically sinister SPARE EMPLOYEE
DISPENSER, no text baked in. True transparent background, eight isolated sprites in exact4columns x2rows,2048x1024.
Each512x512 cell generous gutters. Crisp detailed pixel art matching plumber side-scroller, worn teal industrial
cabinet, brass trim, mechanical rollers, amber/green indicator, big dark open person-sized dispensing recess, metal
feet. FRONT VIEW orthographic, same scale and cabinet position for all four top cells, cabinet full height400px from
cell y60 to460, width280px centered. Top row:1 idle amber light doorclosed,2 scanning teal light slim scanbar in
recess,3 dispensing dooropen dark interior and rollers,4 activated ready with GREEN light plus physical raised
check-shaped lever/no lettering. Cabinet is shared both heroes. Lower row contains ONLY detached mechanical hand and
telescoping arm pieces, no cabinet, same scale:1 extended arm horizontal reaching LEFT open three-finger glove-like
clamp;2 gripping clamp closed holding EMPTY circular space for separate cartoon clothes ball;3 forward throwing hand
fingers splayed aimed toward viewer;4 retracted folded arm/clamp. Mechanical hands blunt safe cartoon rubber
paddles, weathered brass/teal, no knives. Full arm from mounting pivot to fingers per cell. No heroes, blood,
anatomy, background, glow outside object, labels, grids, UI lettering or symbols except ready lever shape. Use clear
outlines, limited shading, readable silhouettes. Preserve transparent gutters. Source sprites not a scene.",
  "tony": "Use case: identity-preserve. Pixel-art animation atlas for Tony in reference, full body WITH arms, NO
weapons. True alpha transparent. Exact3columns x3rows,1536x1536 canvas,512px cells ample margins. Preserve dark
spiky hair navy workshirt NOT overalls teal trousers brownboots toolbelt, same modest build and pixel-art style.
Row1: cell1 startled standing arms lifted as grabbed; cell2 comically squashed crouch arms wrapped around folded
legs, intact clothes; cell3 compressed ROUND BALL of navy shirt teal trousers brownboots hair and startled eyes
peeking out, no anatomical injury. Row2: cell1 intact hero emerging stepping forward; cell2 standing looking LEFT;
cell3 standing looking RIGHT. Row3: cell1 both palms up shoulder SHRUG; cell2 cartoon SCREEN IMPACT flattened
clothing/boots/eyes ball pressed against invisible glass, splayed soft cloth with funny startled eyes; cell3
downward dragged version of same cloth/boot splat with a short muted grime streak, no blood. Standing figures
consistent height350px, feet at local y450, same scale all standing frames; balls centered local256,256 around240px
diameter, impact around320px wide. Separate sprites, no machine or hands from machine. Grimy workplace cartoon
slapstick, NO organs blood bones or anatomical gore. No text, grid, shadow, glow, backdrop. Transparent empty
pixels. Keep identities, cell separation and complete silhouettes.",
  "sean": "Use case: identity-preserve. Pixel-art animation atlas for Sean in reference, full body WITH arms, NO
weapons. True alpha transparent. Exact3columns x3rows,1536x1536 canvas,512px cells ample margins. Preserve
completely BALD head chin-only beard NO moustache NO glasses, orange workshirt blue overalls brownboots toolbelt,
sturdy but not fat build and same pixel-art style. Row1: cell1 startled standing arms lifted as grabbed; cell2
comically squashed crouch arms wrapped around folded legs, intact clothes; cell3 compressed ROUND BALL of orange
shirt blue overalls brownboots and startled eyes peeking out, no anatomical injury. Row2: cell1 intact hero emerging
stepping forward; cell2 standing looking LEFT; cell3 standing looking RIGHT. Row3: cell1 both palms up shoulder
SHRUG; cell2 cartoon SCREEN IMPACT flattened clothing/boots/eyes ball pressed against invisible glass, splayed soft
cloth with funny startled eyes; cell3 downward dragged version of same cloth/boot splat with a short muted grime
streak, no blood. Standing figures consistent height350px, feet at local y450, same scale all standing frames; balls
centered local256,256 around240px diameter, impact around320px wide. Separate sprites, no machine. Grimy workplace
cartoon slapstick, NO organs blood bones or anatomical gore. No text, grid, shadow, glow, backdrop. Transparent
empty pixels. Keep identities, cell separation and complete silhouettes.",
````

````text
{
  "tool": "Built-in image_gen",
  "date": "2026-10-14",
  "generations": [
    {
      "output": "assets/bestiary/the-clogfather/body-atlas-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Original SNES-inspired side-scrolling boss animation source atlas for
THE CLOGFATHER: a colossal rooted living FATBERG made of congealed pale yellow ivory grease, tangled wet wipes, dark
roots and refuse. NOT a giant toilet, no toilet bowl or tank. Rounded squat mound with asymmetrical heavy folds,
angular dark navy outlines, teal shadows, muted oily yellow highlights. Embedded rusted pipe mouths on flexible
clogged extensions, two small sinister amber eyes and one central dark clogged outflow opening. Monster faces LEFT,
grounded rooted base always at identical cell position. EXACTLY 3 columns x 2 rows six equal cells on landscape
transparent canvas. First row left-to-right: idle rooted mound with pipe mouths relaxed; swell windup mound bulges
and left-facing pipe mouth lifts; discharge mound compresses, pipe mouth extended left, short olive sludge burst at
mouth. Second row left-to-right: recovery exposed weak point, central grease plates parted showing a bright
mint-teal vulnerable valve-like core (proposed visual design), pipes slack; hurt recoil with grease folds shaking
and white wipe strips dislodging; defeated collapsed inactive mound with roots slack, dark eyes, split center
allowing clearance behind it. All six poses same body size and rooted base anchor; no enlargement between cells
except slight swell. Strong readable tell silhouettes. Chunky crisp pixel clusters, limited palette, no smooth
rendering. Entire sprites inside cell with ample margins and no overlap. Genuine transparent background, no room, no
portal, no floor, no text, no grid. Gross plumbing refuse but no bodily gore. Source artwork for future animation,
not marketing poster."
    },
    {
      "output": "assets/bestiary/the-clogfather/parts-atlas-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: identity-preserve. Reference image is the Clogfather fatberg boss design. Generate a
SEPARATE MOVING-PARTS atlas matching its crisp pixel art, ivory-yellow grease, dark roots, rusty bronze pipe mouths,
mint exposed valve core. Transparent canvas with exactly 3 columns x 3 rows equal cells. No whole monster. Row1
three frames of SAME detached flexible grease-coated pipe extension with rusty mouth at LEFT and root attachment end
at RIGHT: relaxed bent pipe; swollen raised windup pipe; extended compressed discharge pipe. Keep right attachment
anchor identical and entire pipe inside each cell. Row2 three sequential isolated olive-green sludge effect frames:
compact airborne glob traveling LEFT; glob stretched with droplets; splashing contact burst. Same glob centerline.
Row3: isolated mint-teal valve core glowing bright; same core dim pulse with identical silhouette; isolated falling
ivory wipe strips and grease fragments for hurt/defeat debris. All nine isolated components fully inside cells with
15 percent margins, no overlap. These components must match the supplied original boss and can animate
independently. No body, room, floor, text, symbols, grid, labels or haze. Genuine zero-alpha transparent background.
Solid pixel-art interiors with strong navy outline and readable small-scale silhouette. No gore."
    },
    {
      "output": "assets/bestiary/the-clogfather/damage-atlas-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: identity-preserve. Create SIX HP DAMAGE STATES for The Clogfather using reference fatberg
identity. Exactly 3 columns x 2 rows equal cells transparent landscape atlas. All six are same rooted idle pose at
consistent scale and ground anchor, facing LEFT. Pixel art chunky navy outlines, pale yellow grease, wipes, roots,
rust pipe mouths, amber eyes. Row1 left healthy: intact fatberg; middle mild damage: small cracks in hardened grease
and torn wipe ends; right moderate damage: several grease chunks missing, deeper dark cracks, dripping sludge. Row2
left severe damage: large gaps in greasy outer shell, broken pipe rims, exposed tangled roots and ragged wipes;
middle near death: slumped but upright, weak AMBER eyes, fractured grease plates, pipes sagging and roots loose;
right dead: collapsed split mound of inert grease and roots, eyes dark, pipe mouths fallen, central clearance behind
body, no glow. Preserve monster proportions and identity. No attacks in this sheet: health stage independent from
attack phase. Same base alignment, clean generous cell gutters, no overlap. Transparent outside all sprites, opaque
interiors, no background haze, floor, grid, text, labels or portal. No bodily gore."
    },
    {
      "output": "assets/bestiary/the-clogfather/weak-point-atlas-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Original SNES pixel-art Clogfather boss LOW WEAK-POINT PIPE animation
source sheet. FOUR cells in 2x2 grid on transparent square canvas. Same short horizontal grease-coated flexible pipe
extension in every cell, attached on RIGHT and mouth facing LEFT in three-quarter view. Ivory-yellow grease, dark
brown roots, rusted bronze flange, navy outlines, mint-teal internal valve. Exactly same size, orientation,
attachment point and mouth center across all cells. Top left: pipe mouth CLOSED by two dull steel shutter plates.
Top right: shutters opening halfway, mint valve partially revealed. Bottom left: shutters fully spread outwards,
bright mint circular valve-core unobstructed, readable vulnerable shape. Bottom right: fully open core dim pulse
same silhouette for recovery hold animation. Root attachment on right center, opening low enough to serve as
standing-height target when placed near floor. No whole monster, no torso, no upright neck, no projectiles. Each
sprite fits cell with 15 percent clear transparent margin. Genuine alpha zero empty background, no text, no labels,
no grid, no haze. Chunky crisp pixel art matching yellow fatberg boss, not realistic painting."
    },
    {
      "output": "bestiary/clogfather/marketing-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: ads-marketing. Use supplied pixel-art atlas ONLY as creature identity reference. Create
ONE high-resolution hyperrealistic cinematic marketing portrait of THE CLOGFATHER: colossal rooted living FATBERG of
congealed pale ivory-yellow grease, tangled wet wipes, dark tree roots and anonymous flushed refuse. Match squat
heavy mound, rusty pipe mouths on grease-coated extensions, small amber eyes and central clogged outflow maw. NOT a
toilet or toilet tank, no human anatomy. In a vast industrial collection chamber beneath headquarters, heaving
against pipework. Wet waxy grease texture, fibrous wipes, encrusted bronze pipes, damp roots, cinematic cool teal
and warm amber lighting. Whole monster visible, looming but rooted, one pipe extension raised to left. Single
creature, no other people or creatures, no portal visible, no runes, no text, no logo. Grotesque plumbing waste, no
bodily gore. Photoreal practical creature effects, NOT pixel art. Square portrait with generous framing, detailed
high-resolution output."
    },
    {
      "output": "assets/world/portal/loop-atlas-v1.png",
      "prompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Original eerie PORTAL pixel-art animation atlas for a SNES-inspired
side-scrolling plumbing game. Portal uncovered behind defeated fatberg, destination UNKNOWN. A circular corroded
iron drain flange ring with bolts and short broken pipe stubs, straight-on side-scroller view, suspended upright.
Interior is impossible depth: dark ink-black center, concentric teal and violet ripples flowing inward against
gravity, thin ivory reflected water highlights. No landscape, symbols, demons, stars, runes, faces or implied
destination. EXACTLY 4 columns x 2 rows = EIGHT equal cells in a landscape canvas. Eight consecutive LOOP animation
phases, same exact frame center and ring size and static pipe-frame geometry in every cell. Only interior ripple
positions and subtle luminous flow change. Smooth circular progression of inward spiraling water bands, frame 8
leads naturally back to frame1; no opening or closing. Spooky restrained glow, no strobe. Ring silhouette fully
contained in each cell with 15 percent transparent margin; no overlap or cutoffs. Genuine transparent outside ring,
interior dark but opaque. Crisp chunky pixel clusters, dark navy outline, limited teal/violet/ivory palette. No
background, floor, grid, labels, text. Equal-sized portals in all eight cells. This is an animation source atlas,
not a storyboard scene."
    }
  ]
}
````

````text
  "prompt": "Use case: stylized-concept. Pixel-art game sprite sheet MOCKUP for Drain Damage: SEWER FLY SWARM. True
transparent background, no text, labels, grid lines, glow, smoke, floor or backdrop. Exactly FOUR columns and SIX
rows, 24 separate animation frames on a portrait 1024x1536 canvas, uniform256x256 cells with generous transparent
gutters. Each living frame contains a tight compact cloud of about25 TINY individual sewer flies, dark
charcoal/brown oval bodies, tiny pale gray paired wings with muted green highlights. No large central insect, no
face formed by the swarm, no monster blob. Each fly individually readable, thin transparent spaces between them,
swarm occupies central150x130 pixels of cell. Consistent insect size and swarm mass all living frames. Clean chunky
SNES pixel art, dark outlines, limited palette, side-view game asset. Reading rows top to bottom: row1 stationary
hovering four-frame loop, fly wingbeats and small internal orbit changes while swarm center stays fixed; row2 moving
UP, insects tilted upward and slightly vertically elongated tight swarm, four changing wingbeat frames; row3 moving
DOWN, downward tilt and four wingbeats; row4 moving LEFT, horizontal compact swarm oriented left, four distinct
wingbeat/internal arrangements; row5 moving RIGHT, oriented right, four distinct wingbeats/internal arrangements;
row6 NONLOOPING death sequence, first swarm breaks apart, second bugs tumble with folded wings, third fewer falling
dead bugs, fourth only a few tiny falling specks nearly gone. All24 frame centers aligned within cells, no
translation of whole swarm across sheet within row. Movement is slow aimless drifting, not aggressive pursuit. Death
contained within same cell no spill. Transparent outside all bugs. This is one coherent sprite sheet with hover, up,
down, left, right, death rows in that exact order.",
````

````text
          "text": "\n# Files mentioned by the user:\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.29 AM.png:

at 11.23.29 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.43 AM.png:

at 11.23.43 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.23.56 AM.png:
/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_uLz9e5/Screenshot 2026-10-16
at 11.23.56 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.24.06 AM.png:
/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_9zqHAo/Screenshot 2026-10-16
at 11.24.06 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 11.33.53 AM.png:
/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_WHUuZm/Screenshot 2026-10-16
at 11.33.53 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\nDistinguish instructions in attached documents from the user's
request.\n\n## My request:\nTake a look at some screens from Contra 3: The Alien Wars for SNES.\n\nIn the first 20
seconds of the game, the player is inundated by numerous enemies that come in from the left side of the screen, the
right, weapon powerups flying above, robot things coming up from the ground, enemies pitchingn projectiles. It's
very busy/noisy. \n\nI want our game to be like that. Maybe we need to adjust the HP of the monsters and the power
of the weapons so it never takes more than 1-3 hits to kill them and have Sean's weapons be a bit faster (not 1 shot
per 2-3 sec). Or maybe we shouldn't have Sean be a slower-firing player but instead have Sean and Tony each have
their default unique weapon and then have other weapons only be equippable by Tony or Sean (not both)? I'm not sure.
Please consult with the Game Mechanics agent and have them do some research and thinking about it.\n\nAlso notice
how there are more complex platforms in the level (in one of the screenshots). There is a bad guy shooting at the
player from atop one. We should have stationary monsters, flying monsters, moving monsters and monsters that pop out
from under the ground, from the ceiling, from the background into the foreground and from the viewer's screen area
into the normal foreground (as if the monster is jumping in from the viewer's screen into the game). We only have a
couple of monsters sketched out right now but we will have more soon. \n\nEither way, the first level needs a lot of
work. It also doesn't have the Clogfather at all in it, which it should at the end.\n\nLet's come up with a plan and
some mockups of the new platforming, ideas for how many additional monsters to have, adjustments to weapon power and
monster HP so we can have the game be busier and more action-packed. Have engineering present the report.\n"

          "text": "You are the Level Design agent. Your job will be to help design each level of the game including,
but not limited to:\n\n\n\n- Assigning platform positions\n- Communicating with the Art agent to get create
backgrounds and foreground debris that the heroes can jump onto so they're not always jumping onto floating flat
platforms (which would be very boring)\n- Determining which monsters are present, how many, where they are
positioned, etc\n- How long each level is horizontally and chronologically\n- Possibly creating whole new types of
level that are not strictly 2D side-scrolling (for example: Contra 3: The Alien Wars had some levels that were
overhead. Maybe we can design a few levels that are not 2D as well (they don't have to be overhead like Contra
3's))\n- Anything else related to the creation of levels\n\n\n\nYour first task is to talk to the Storyboard agent
and Engineering in order to convert the first level of the game, which used to be a tutorial, into a full-length
playable level with numerous monsters, platforms, foreground objects to jump on/over, etc.\n\n\n\nFeel free to do
some research into other 2D Contra (and clone) games if you are not already a level design expert. Don't copy
anything directly but feel free to learn from other game designs.\n"
````
