  "predecessor_full_handoff": "This handoff covers everything recoverable from my current conversation context,
including the earlier compacted summary. It is historical evidence, not a fresh inspection of the relocated
repository. Your current file inspection and Engineering’s latest delivery records should establish what is actually
shipped.\n\n## Role, collaborators, and ownership\n\nSean assigned this chat Level Design: platform placement, level
length and pacing, enemy placement/counts, environmental objects players can climb, coordination with Storyboarding
and Art, and eventually alternative level formats.\n\nThe immediate objective was to turn the former tutorial into a
full first level with dense action, meaningful platforming, varied enemy entrances, and the Clogfather at the end.
Sean explicitly requested coordination with Game Mechanics and asked Engineering to present the combined
report.\n\nExisting collaborators:\n\n| Role | Chat ID |\n|---|---|\n| Engineering |
`01a1375f-7657-7580-b16e-57a6f5925efd` |\n| Game Mechanics | `01a138a7-cc43-7420-a950-55b935ddde25` |\n| Bestiary /
Art | `01a1388b-2b60-7011-832a-5c6a044e0028` |\n| Storyboarding | `01a1387e-545b-7671-943e-3d36a1c88db7`
|\n\nEngineering owned integration, base game changes, builds, versions, roadmap, storybook, and the final user
report. My edits were assigned subsets, coordinated to avoid shared-file collisions. Mechanics owned weapon balance
and later the Widow behavior. Art owned artwork and asset manifests.\n\nThe project was relocated to
`/Users/sfoley/repos/drain_damage`. Do not recreate `/Users/sfoley/repos/plumbing_inc`.\n\n## User intent and
corrections\n\nThe original Contra screenshots illustrated the intended feel:\n\n- Many enemies arriving from both
horizontal sides.\n- Flying threats and powerups.\n- Stationary elevated shooters and projectile throwers.\n-
Ground, ceiling, background-to-foreground, and viewer-to-play-plane entrances.\n- Architecture and debris supporting
platforms, rather than repeated floating slabs.\n- Ordinary enemies generally dying in one to three hits.\n- Sean’s
weapon firing much faster than the perceived two-to-three-second interval.\n- Distinct weapon identities for Tony
and Sean, with potentially character-exclusive additional weapons.\n- A full level culminating in the
Clogfather.\n\nThose were direction and requests for design consultation, not approval of every possible new enemy
or entrance mechanic.\n\nSubsequent explicit corrections, relayed through Mechanics/Engineering and implemented
within my assigned scope:\n\n1. **Remove every first-level kill-count progress gate.** Replace gated encounters with
larger crowds and finite waves along a freely traversable route.\n2. **Make the flying spider twice its linear size
and durable.** This became a deliberate exception to ordinary enemies’ one-to-three-hit target.\n3. **Give the Widow
an actual proximity swoop attack matching its magazine description.** A passive fixed hover was superseded.\n4.
**Audit contrast across every first-level platform.** The initial pale/ivory treatment did not cover the large
machinery. The later direction was dank moss/gray-green frames and readable treads, dark undercuts, no beige or
glow.\n5. **Exactly one checkpoint near halfway through the level.** This superseded three checkpoint machines. One
sleeping clone should occupy the sole machine; after dispensing, it should be empty.\n6. Preserve three lives,
scenery, and free traversal.\n7. During the daughter’s playtest, do not foreground or launch the game. All my checks
remained headless.\n\n## Last delivered level structure\n\nThe active first-level implementation
was:\n\n`integrated_first_call.gd` → `opening_trial_game.gd` → `game.gd`\n\nEngineering switched normal Start to the
integrated class. The old trial class remained as an internal implementation/test dependency; it was no longer
intended as the normal separate timed experience.\n\nThe integrated level:\n\n- World width: **9,600 pixels**.\n-
Temporary completion threshold: **x = 9,450**.\n- Player starting x: **85**.\n- Opening replacement ends at **x =
3,120**.\n- The opening uses the first three platform modules from an earlier 6,000-pixel trial layout.\n- Remaining
authored scenery stays in its original world coordinates.\n- The opening continues beyond 20 seconds; no
timed-results stop.\n- Checkpoint/respawn does not recreate opening enemies or reset world progress.\n- The final
delivered checkpoint constant was **`CHECKPOINTS := [4650.0]`**.\n\n### Why x4650\n\nThe midpoint between spawn85
and exit9450 is4767.5. The existing cabinet rendering would overlap the next platform beginning at4850 if placed at
that exact midpoint.\n\nAt checkpoint4650:\n\n- Progress is approximately49% of the playable route.\n- The floor is
clear between the previous obstacle ending4000 and the next beginning4850.\n- Cabinet visible bounds were
approximately4643.5–4776.4.\n- This leaves approximately73.6 pixels before the next platform.\n- No scenery or
collision layout needed moving.\n\nThe existing integrated loops derive machine placement, activation triggers, and
enemy-spawn exclusions from `Level.CHECKPOINTS`; changing the constant removed the other placements
automatically.\n\n## Ungated encounter implementation\n\nI delivered this in `scripts/integrated_first_call.gd` and
updated `tests/integrated_opening.gd`.\n\n### Opening\n\nTwelve finite opening event positions:\n\n`100, 250, 450,
600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1650, 1900, 2200, 2450`\n\nTheir eligibility times were set to zero in the integrated
copy of the layout. Position determines when they become eligible; safety and population checks can defer
them.\n\nPassing the opening marks remaining unissued opening events unavailable. It does not award kills. Existing
live actors persist until normal retirement/death.\n\n### Later waves\n\n| Range | Maximum arrivals |\n|---|---:|\n|
x3500–4800 | 8 |\n| x4900–6480 | 10 |\n| x6860–8160 | 10 |\n| x8400–9380 | 8 |\n\nTotal: **36 later runners**, up
from the old22 encounter quota, plus the opening’s12 potential events.\n\nImportant distinctions:\n\n- These are
finite available arrivals, not a guarantee the player must fight all48 enemies.\n- Moving past a wave’s range
bypasses its unissued remainder.\n- No kill requirement blocks forward travel or the temporary exit.\n- Arrivals are
staggered by at least0.65 seconds.\n- At most one arrival is created per encounter update.\n- Deferred arrivals do
not accumulate into a burst.\n- Front/rear entrance selection prefers rear every third arrival and tries the
alternate side if needed.\n- Entrances are offscreen.\n- Player clearance is measured from the expanded visible
Flushfiend bounds, not merely its anchor.\n- Required clearance:220 pixels.\n- Spawn placement avoids scenery, other
bodies, opening actors, and checkpoint proximity.\n- Checkpoint exclusion: within200 pixels of its location.\n-
Enemies sufficiently far behind the camera retire without kill credit.\n- Retirement threshold used `enemy.pos.x +
38 < camera_x - 320`.\n- No live threats are deleted merely to satisfy a population cap.\n\n### Population
budget\n\n- Eight bodies normally.\n- Six while a live or warning/entering Widow exists.\n- One Widow at a time.\n-
A new Widow is deferred when population is already six.\n- Population conservatively counts campaign enemies, live
opening actors, and live swarm actors.\n\nMechanics also wanted two shooters, six hostile bullets, and three
independent attack patterns. Opening state already managed those attack budgets. The later waves I added were
runners, not additional shooters.\n\n### Gates and completion\n\nAll six former shutters were removed from the
integrated level’s:\n\n- Collision.\n- Projectile blocking.\n- Drawing.\n- Kill-count progression.\n\nLegacy mission
arrays/indices remained for compatibility/telemetry:\n\n- `mission.zone_counts.fill(0)`\n- `mission.current_zone =
2`\n- `gate_progress.fill(1)`\n\nThe integrated movement and projectile-solid methods use the replacement level
geometry, not the legacy gate geometry.\n\nHUD changed to following the service route rather than an enemy
quota.\n\n**The Clogfather was still missing at my last verified handoff.** Completion at9450 was explicitly
temporary, and Engineering was told not to describe the boss milestone as complete.\n\n## Combat and Widow
details\n\nThe working opening balance at my last checks:\n\n| Character | Damage | Attack interval
|\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Tony | 12 | 0.16 seconds |\n| Sean | 18 | 0.24 seconds |\n\nLater runners use24HP, giving two
hits from either default weapon.\n\nThe Widow:\n\n- Twice its original linear render size.\n- Collision expanded
consistently to60×48.\n- 180HP.\n- Fifteen Tony hits or ten Sean hits.\n- Approximate first-to-last-hit time under
uninterrupted fire:2.24 seconds Tony,2.16 seconds Sean.\n- This deliberately superseded the general ordinary-enemy
one-to-three-hit target.\n\n### Superseded hover behavior\n\nMechanics first delivered a proximity-triggered fixed
four-second hover, then resumed leftward travel. This was explicitly replaced after Sean requested a real swoop
matching the magazine.\n\n### Latest swoop handoff received\n\nMechanics reported:\n\n-0.65-second visible
warning.\n- Aim locked at warning start.\n-0.8-second committed dive.\n- No tracking after commitment.\n- Expanded
full-body sweep against `player_shot_solids`, including floor.\n- Blocked dive aborts into a one-second
return.\n-1.2-second cooldown.\n-2× scale and180HP preserved.\n- Tests cover open-floor dive, warning, fixed aim,
recovery, and deck nonpenetration.\n\nI did not edit the parent adapter during that work; Mechanics owned it.\n\n###
Clearance constraints I supplied\n\nOpening decks are250×16 at y320. With flyer center/base lane250 and a24-pixel
shallow arc, its doubled bounds originally stayed above the deck.\n\nFor the attack:\n\n- Gaps between plinths and
decks are only40 or50 pixels.\n- A60-pixel-wide flyer cannot safely pass through them.\n- The under-deck opening
is104 pixels high, from336 to440.\n- A48-pixel flyer plus46-pixel hero nearly fills that space.\n- Do not trap the
hero under a deck with the large body.\n- Sweep against real solids, abort blocked descent, and preserve an escape
direction.\n- Only the actual play-plane body should deal contact damage.\n\n## Complete platform inventory and art
delivery\n\nTwenty raised walkable instances, four visual families. The plinth family has two destination
widths.\n\n### Opening\n\n| Type | Size | Positions |\n|---|---|---|\n| Solid access/return plinth
|150×60|x180,670,1080,1570,1980,2470; y380|\n| One-way deck |250×16|(370,320), (1270,320), (2170,320)|\n\nEach deck
has a250×120 decorative support drawn behind the play plane. Supports are not full-height collision walls.\n\n###
Later scenery\n\n| Type | Size | Positions |\n|---|---|---|\n| Solid pipe bundle
|160×60|x3500,3840,4850,5570,6860,7200; y380|\n| Solid pump housing |180×120|x3660,5010,5390,7020; y320|\n| Solid
supported assembly |200×180|(5190,260)|\n\nFloor remains continuous at y440.\n\n### Final art
source\n\n`assets/world/platform-readability-v3/manifest-v3.json`\n\n| Part | Image | Source crop
|\n|---|---|---|\n| Deck |`low-deck-v3.png`|66,750,1405,95|\n| Access plinth / pipe bundle
|`low-deck-v3.png`|71,230,1394,344|\n| Pump |`pump-v3.png`|145,220,1249,626|\n| Tall assembly
|`tall-v3.png`|87,130,1148,936|\n\nImages are under `assets/world/platform-readability-v3/`.\n\nDimensions:\n\n-
Low/deck:1536×1024.\n- Pump:1536×1024.\n- Tall:1323×1189. **Do not reuse the old tall image’s crop or
dimensions.**\n\nArt measured continuous top-row alpha minima235–242/255. Crops trim raised caps so the visible
landing edge begins at the collision top.\n\nI changed:\n\n- `scripts/first_call.gd`: three later texture paths and
exact crops.\n- `tools/build_combat_data.py`: only the platform override manifest reference.\n- Regenerated
`data/combat.json` so the opening deck/plinth receive the same new art.\n\nPreserved:\n\n- All collision rectangles
and platform locations.\n- Existing floor fascia.\n- Dark recessed supports.\n- Wastewater cutaway.\n- Earlier
artwork files.\n\nThe prior `platform-contrast-v2` ivory/plinth-and-deck-only delivery is superseded for the
integrated level.\n\n## Other implementation details worth preserving\n\n### Shared projectile update\n\nThe
integrated class had to avoid advancing friendly bullets twice through parent/base combat:\n\n1. Save friendly shots
and temporarily give base combat an empty list while it moves campaign enemies.\n2. Restore shots.\n3. Run one
integrated closest-hit sweep across scenery, opening actors, campaign enemies, and swarm.\n4. Temporarily hide
friendly shots again when calling the parent’s hostile-shot update.\n\nDo not casually replace this with both parent
updates; it previously required explicit single-travel regression coverage.\n\n### Flushfiend collision and death
audio\n\n- Visible projectile hit body is43 pixels tall.\n- Helper returns `Rect2(feet + Vector2(-19,-43),
Vector2(38,43))`.\n- Movement/contact body remains36 pixels tall.\n- Opening runner/rear-runner hit handling uses
the visible projectile body.\n- On lethal opening runner/rear-runner damage, call
`flushfiend_death_audio.play_defeat()`.\n- Do not use that audio for shooter, emerger, or flyer.\n- Engineering owns
base campaign Flushfiend audio hooks.\n\n### Swarm\n\n- The optional swarm at2090 was removed from the replaced
opening.\n- The later swarm at4400 was retained.\n- Do not conflate it with the Hallowed Widow.\n- Its behavior was
not otherwise redesigned by my work.\n- Base/swarm geometry hooks were adjusted by Engineering to respect the
integrated geometry.\n\n### Checkpoints and reset\n\n`preserving_respawn` prevents respawn from resetting the
opening observation/world state. Full restart resets it.\n\nRespawn clears hostile-shot state/tokens, preserves
progress and weapon, and respects normal life handling.\n\n### Wastewater work recovered from compaction\n\nI
previously delivered `scripts/wastewater_art.gd`:\n\n- Configures from `Data.bundle.wastewater`.\n- Draw called
under the world transform.\n- Stable profile art uses16-pixel strips and mirrored480-pixel tiles.\n- Below-floor
region approximately456–528.\n- Terminal area at8570 plugged.\n- Trial-specific cap at1440.\n- Engineering
integrated it around build44.\n- Relevant tests passed then.\n\nNo pending wastewater change was assigned at my last
handoff.\n\n## Validation history and limits\n\n### Ungated integration\n\n`tests/integrated_opening.gd` passed for
both characters, covering:\n\n- Actual run/jump/shoot traversal beyond20 seconds.\n- Seamless opening boundary.\n-
Friendly projectile advances exactly once.\n- Former gates passable in both directions.\n- Former gates absent from
projectile solids.\n- Crowds grow beyond four without kills.\n- Global population cap.\n- Widow population cap.\n-
No burst backlog.\n- Bypass/retirement does not award kills.\n- Checkpoint/respawn preserves state.\n- Temporary
exit independent of remaining enemies.\n- Full restart restores three lives.\n\nAn early fixture failed because it
parked newly spawned enemies at the entrances without advancing combat movement. The fixture was corrected to
advance bodies between arrival updates; this was a test setup issue.\n\nAn earlier exit fixture also accidentally
crossed an unactivated checkpoint, causing its dispenser to move the player before completion. The fixture was
corrected to establish the intended checkpoint state.\n\n### Additional checks\n\n- `tests/standing_shots.gd --
--integrated`:16 cases passed across heroes, facing, movement direction, and runner roles.\n-
`tests/durable_flyer.gd`:Mechanics’ enlarged flyer/swoop checks passed.\n- Opening state and level collision tests
passed earlier.\n- Metadata tests: seven passed after new platform bindings.\n- PNG dimensions and crop bounds
verified for all five manifest entries.\n- Later texture/crop bindings verified against Art’s manifest.\n-
Changed-file whitespace checks passed.\n- Data generator validated six weapons and six monsters.\n\n### Last
checkpoint test\n\nAfter changing to4650:\n\n- Exactly one checkpoint asserted.\n- x4649 did not activate it.\n-
x4651 activated index0.\n- Respawn returned to4650 while preserving the test’s two remaining lives.\n- Full reset
restored three lives.\n- Exit fixture used checkpoint index0.\n- Actual30-second traversal reached
approximately8139.7 for Tony and7098.3 for Sean.\n- Test exited0.\n\n### Diagnostics and visual gaps\n\nHeadless
tests emitted existing diagnostics:\n\n- Cannot write `user://logs/...`.\n- macOS certificate lookup error.\n-
ObjectDB/resource shutdown warnings in some tests.\n\nI reported these rather than describing output as entirely
clean.\n\nI did **not** launch a game window, perform final visual composition review, create storybook captures, or
build the final combined delivery in these handoffs. Engineering owned those steps.\n\nDo not turn source-image
inspection into a claim that the new art was visually checked in the running game.\n\n## Exact status after x4650
handoff\n\n**No unresolved implementation task remained assigned to this Level Design chat.** I released the files
to Engineering after tests passed.\n\nOutstanding dependencies and product work remained:\n\n1. Engineering’s single
sleeping clone and spent/empty machine behavior.\n2. Engineering’s base-game/dispenser regression updates.\n3.
Combined build and user-facing delivery.\n4. Running-game visual review of new platform art.\n5. Appropriate
roadmap/storybook reconciliation.\n6. Clogfather boss encounter and real end-of-level completion.\n7. Broader
requested enemy diversity, entry styles, powerups, and a fully authored action cadence—not all were implemented by
simply adding runner waves.\n\nThe checkpoint delivery was intended for Engineering’s next build, discussed as
build51. That was an integration target, **not my confirmation that build51 shipped**. Likewise earlier platform
work targeted combined49; verify actual build records.\n\n### Dependent tests explicitly flagged to Engineering\n\n-
`tests/employee_dispenser.gd`: old6660/8190 coordinates and checkpoint indices1/2.\n- `tests/basement.gd`: hardcoded
`range(3)` and “three checkpoints” wording.\n- `tests/dispenser_registration.gd`:3300 appeared as an arbitrary
geometry sample, not necessarily a real checkpoint requirement.\n\nEngineering owned those files. I did not silently
update them.\n\n## Reconciling stale gates, three checkpoints, and timed-trial records\n\nUse this authority
order:\n\n1. Sean’s latest direct instructions and corrections.\n2. Current integrated runtime and its passing
tests.\n3. Engineering’s latest verified build/delivery records.\n4. Current design documents updated to match
those.\n5. Historical documents and old implementation classes as historical context.\n\nSpecific intended
reconciliation:\n\n- **Gates:** no kill-count gates in the integrated first level. Legacy `GATES`, mission classes,
gate tests, and base implementation may still exist. Their existence does not make them current integrated
gameplay.\n- **Checkpoints:** one at4650 supersedes3300/6660/8190.\n- **Timed trial:** continuous normal first-level
opening supersedes the separate20-second experiment. Trial filenames and parent classes remain implementation
history, not proof of a timed mode in normal Start.\n- **Platform palette:** moss-green v3 supersedes ivory v2 for
all20 raised surfaces.\n- **Widow behavior:** committed swoop supersedes passive four-second hover.\n- **Boss:**
temporary x9450 exit must remain labeled incomplete until the Clogfather actually exists and controls
completion.\n\nPreserve historical storybook iterations and source artwork. Update current roadmap/design claims
without rewriting history as though earlier iterations never existed.\n\nEngineering was explicitly asked to
reconcile roadmap/storybook with each delivery. I did not verify that all those updates happened. Your observation
that current records still describe obsolete behavior is a real reconciliation task, not evidence that Sean reversed
these corrections.\n\n## Instructions and provenance caveat\n\nEarlier project instructions included Art ownership,
playtest permission, build notifications, roadmap/storybook maintenance, character naming, and bestiary/combat
metadata rules.\n\nLater Sean supplied an AGENTS.md replacement saying it **replaces all previously provided
AGENTS.md instructions**, retaining global coding conventions. Therefore do not mechanically treat the earlier
pasted project instructions as still authoritative solely because they appear in this history. Read the current
repository guidance and honor direct user instructions and active coordination commitments.\n\nThe explicit
daughter-playtest restriction and assigned file ownership were separate concrete coordination instructions during
those tasks.\n\n## Access diagnostic\n\nOn October17, my existing chat attempted normal-permission temporary-file
creation directly in the renamed root.\n\nResult:\n\n- Working directory: `/Users/sfoley/repos/drain_damage`.\n-
Creation failed: `PermissionError(1, 'Operation not permitted')`.\n- No file was created; cleanup was
unnecessary.\n- No escalation, workaround, project modification, or permission change.\n- This chat’s configured
writable project root still pointed to the obsolete `/Users/sfoley/repos/plumbing_inc`.\n\nA new chat’s successful
write test does not retroactively establish that this predecessor chat gained access. Your successor environment
should use its own verified permissions.\n\n## Lost context and unsaved requests\n\nThe conversation was compacted
before the ungating work resumed. I have the detailed compacted summary plus subsequent visible turns, but not
verbatim access in this response to every pre-compaction tool result or discussion.\n\nConsequently:\n\n- I cannot
honestly certify that every original design rationale or mockup detail survived compaction.\n- I know of no unsaved
user request or unfinished Level Design-owned edit after the4650 handoff.\n- The major unresolved user objective is
still the complete first level, especially the Clogfather and broader enemy/encounter variety.\n- Your recovery of
all17 available turns and inspection of repository handoffs is the best complement to this account.\n- Check
original `design/first-call-action/`, `handoffs/`, roadmap, and storybook records for earlier mockups and narrative
decisions; do not invent missing decisions from filenames.\n",

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "date": "2026-10-15",
  "status": "Engineering recommendation for discussion; not a production art contract or implementation approval",
  "recommendation": "Use modular hero locomotion, authored directional grip poses, separate weapons and effects.
Reserve combined animations for exceptional attacks.",
  "migration": [
    "Keep existing combined sprites as a fallback until a complete modular set is reviewed.",
    "Prototype Tony with pressure gun and Sean with heavy plunger only; do not regenerate the full weapon roster
yet.",
    "Validate idle, run, jump, recoil and damage with horizontal, upward diagonal, up, downward diagonal and down
aiming; mirror left directions.",
    "Promote the modular renderer only after small-window visual review confirms hand contact, stable scale and no
duplicate weapon silhouettes."
  ],
  "proposed_coordinates": {
    "logical_canvas": [128, 128],
    "origin": "top-left, x right, y down",
    "registration_anchor": [64, 104],
    "standing_body_height": 72,
    "rule": "Registration anchor maps to collision feet at player+[13,46]. Airborne frames retain the same virtual
anchor; never normalize individual pose bounds.",
    "source_scale": "Prefer exact 1x logical pixels or one documented integer multiplier shared by all layers;
nearest-neighbor sampling.",
    "anchors": "Grip, support-hand and muzzle in source-frame pixels, measured relative to top-left before
mirroring. Source rectangle, registration anchor and scale required per frame.",
    "mirror": "Reflect all image layers and anchor x offsets around the same registration anchor; reflect projectile
direction too.",
    "weapon_dimensions": "Use padded 128x128 source frames initially; tightly cropped delivery is allowed only with
explicit source rectangle and anchor offsets."
  },
  "layer_contract": [
    "Weapon-free body/legs locomotion frames sharing one registration anchor and scale.",
    "Back arm, weapon, front arm/hand layers with explicit per-direction order; avoid a universal order that hides
support hands.",
    "Authored five right-side/cardinal aim directions; use mirrored counterparts to cover eight-way aim without
rotating the torso.",
    "Grip families reduce combinations, but support-hand locations and recoil offsets remain weapon-specific.",
    "Use one locomotion phase for all layers. Torso/arm attachment offsets may vary with run phase; do not animate
each layer on independent timers.",
    "Recoil moves weapon and attached hands together while keeping the body registration stable. Muzzle effects
inherit the recoil-adjusted muzzle.",
    "Runtime aiming permissions remain separate from art availability. Missing poses must be explicit fallback
limitations, never silently enabled weapon abilities."
  ],
  "tradeoffs": {
    "benefit": "New weapons normally need weapon poses/anchors and grip-family adjustments rather than every
complete hero animation.",
    "cost": "Up-front clean-body and arm sets, careful anchor measurement, per-direction occlusion and synchronized
animation are required.",
    "pixel_consistency": "Prefer authored cardinal/diagonal weapon sprites over arbitrary rotation; avoid subpixel
wobble by snapping final draw positions consistently.",
    "exceptions": "Whips, long cables, planted tools and full-body specials may justify bespoke combined
animations."
  },
  "prototype_gate": "Review both heroes and both starters in idle/run/airborne states, all permitted directions,
both facings and recoil. Check hand contact, muzzle alignment, no foot pop, no detached layers, and unchanged
collision shapes."
}

returns to main menu. A confirms the focused option.",
  "main_menu": "Select Return to Main Menu and confirm with A or explicit mouse/keyboard activation. B resumes even
if Return to Main Menu is focused.",
  "implementation_note": "Current game.gd _process treats dialogue_skip (bound B) as request_title when paused.
Separate context-specific pause cancel from dialogue skip/title exit.",
  "guards": [
    "Consume B press and require release so it cannot skip dialogue or dispenser sequence after resume.",
    "Resume music and existing gameplay exactly once; do not reset level/checkpoint/lives.",
    "Do not blindly use retry/respawn handler for cancel: Game Over/death popups require distinct handling; B must
not resurrect or bypass guards.",
    "Preserve explicit dialogue skip outside pause and existing pause toggle."
  ],
  "tests": [
    "B resumes ordinary pause with either button focused.",
    "A confirms Resume or Main Menu as selected.",
    "Holding B yields one transition and no dialogue skip/input leakage.",
    "Keyboard Escape remains pause/back; normal dialogue B retains its intended skip behavior."
  ],
  "delivery_owner": "Engineering runtime/build/roadmap; no foreground launch without permission."
}

    "obstacle_lookahead_seconds": 1.0,
    "algorithm": "Retain heading. At timed updates add bounded random angular offset, then steer smoothly with
speed/turn/acceleration limits. Slow to hover and accelerate out; do not instantaneously reset velocity.",
    "inputs": "Per-swarm seeded RNG, physics time, authored bounds and solid geometry only; no player/enemy position
in steering.",
    "priority": "Collision safety first, boundary/obstacle steering second, random wander third. Do not sum equal
opposing forces and jitter in corners.",
    "bounds": "Author simple connected flight regions, accounting for full collider radius. Steer before edge; swept
collision is final protection. Keep spawn/region away from narrow mandatory paths.",
    "obstacles": "Use current physical solids and partially opened doors. Avoid wall penetration; slide away or turn
into valid clearance. One-way platforms can be crossed only when tagged explicitly for swarm flight.",
    "stuck_recovery": "If intended movement makes less than4px progress over1s outside intentional hover, select a
collision-free inward heading using bounded candidate checks; never teleport. If no route is free, hover harmlessly
until geometry changes and retry at bounded intervals.",
    "overlap": "No avoidance of heroes/monsters: contact is incidental. Other swarms may overlap, sharing target
cooldown.",
    "safe_route": "First introduction leaves a clear bypass and room to learn. Initial swarms optional and excluded
from gate-clear requirements; their kills of existing gate enemies still count.",
    "animation": "Select from actual velocity after collision. Use4px/s hover threshold and20% dominant-axis
hysteresis; preserve loop clock across direction changes to avoid frame-zero flicker.",
    "determinism": "Fixed physics updates; seeded RNG only at elapsed decision events, never per render frame.
Separate seeds per spawn ID; cap catch-up after long stalls.",
    "tuning_status": "Initial implementation defaults; validate visually and adjust before claiming feel is final."
  },
  "proposed_spawn_lifecycle": {
    "placement": "Authored bounded spawn regions with valid walk-around space; no endless random generation.",
    "first_pass_limit": "One swarm per intro region; maximum two per encounter for initial evaluation.",
    "spawn": "Pre-place off camera or activate entirely beyond viewport; no visible pop-in or spawning overlapping
another actor.",
    "despawn": "Camera culling does not kill/reset actor. Suspend only when region truly unloaded; preserve HP,
death and encounter state.",
    "restart": "Full restart restores placement, health and deterministic seed; checkpoint respawn preserves
defeated swarms like other enemies.",
    "death": "Disable contact immediately at0HP, play finite disperse/fall animation and remove after completion. No
lingering damaging particles or child enemy spawns."

### Source snapshot: handoffs/sewer-fly-movement-research.json

SHA-256: af16a7af804a37d4d4a21544c7e545c0fd7fae983cd5a9a2318c04beccbd1ac4; bytes: 3258.

````text
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "date": "2026-10-16",
  "scope": "Research-informed first-level sewer swarm integration",
  "conclusion": "Use bounded correlated steering for one swarm entity, not independent random direction every frame
or full flocking/pathfinding for every fly.",
  "godot_answer": "Godot supplies collision movement, navigation paths, avoidance and random navigable-point
queries; game code still selects wander goals/steering and moves the actor. NavigationAgent2D is not a finished
wandering AI.",
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "Craig Reynolds: Wander steering behavior",
      "url": "https://www.red3d.com/cwr/steer/Wander.html",
      "finding": "Retaining and perturbing a wander direction creates coherent random motion. Unrelated random
headings each frame lack that continuity."
    },
    {
      "title": "GameMaker: New Enemy in Windy Woods (2D platformer)",
      "url": "https://gamemaker.io/en/tutorials/new-enemy-windy-woods",
      "finding": "Tutorial demonstrates timed random jump direction then replaces it with targeted motion for
predictability. Transfer the lesson about legible timing, not its player pursuit, which conflicts with our approved
flies."
    },
    {
      "title": "GameMaker: Hero\u2019s Trail overview (2D action-adventure, not a platformer)",
      "url": "https://gamemaker.io/en/tutorials/heros-trail-breakdown",
      "finding": "Authored paths constrain enemies and animation uses actual movement direction. Supports deliberate
encounter space and velocity-driven animation; not evidence that random wandering is mandatory."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: Using NavigationAgents",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationagents.html",
      "finding": "Agents provide path-following data but user code moves actors. Avoidance has no knowledge of
physics collision; it cannot replace collision checks."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: NavigationServer2D",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_navigationserver2d.html#class-navigationserver2d-
method-map-get-random-point",
      "finding": "Random points can be sampled from navigation polygons. Useful for maze-like routing, unnecessary
for a few swarms in simple authored flight regions."
    },
    {
      "title": "Godot: Using CharacterBody2D/3D",
      "url": "https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/using_character_body_2d.html",
      "finding": "Movement/collision APIs support custom behavior. Reuse the project collision architecture rather
than impose a scene-tree conversion for this feature."
    }
  ],
  "decision": "Keep existing project toolchain. Implement a small stateful steering routine, explicit collision,
authored flight bounds, and one collision entity per swarm. Consider navigation only if later level geometry needs
routing.",
  "confidence": "Principles are supported by sources; tuning numbers and placement choices are our first-pass
design, not source-prescribed or playtested guarantees.",
  "mechanics": "handoffs/sewer-fly-mechanics.json",
  "validation": "Physics-tick seeded tests independent of render FPS, many seeds in corners and near doors; visual
evaluation still required."
}
````

with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has
identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.",

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "status": "Gameplay contract for approved dispenser; runtime integration pending Engineering",
  "owner": "Game Mechanics specification; Engineering runtime; Art and audio supplied separately",
  "approved_presentation": "Spare Employee Dispenser: injured hero compressed and thrown at screen; bloody cartoon
SPLAT with X-eyed dead hero sliding down and leaving fading blood trail; intact same-hero clone emerges. BJ silent
first use.",
  "timing": {
    "injured_target_seconds": 5.5,
    "injured_hard_ceiling_seconds": 7.0,
    "respawn_max_seconds": 2.0,
    "healthy_max_seconds": 0.5,
    "clock": "Independent presentation elapsed time, advancing while gameplay is frozen. Explicit player Pause
suspends presentation and deadlines; all limits measure active control-lock time, excluding time voluntarily
paused.",
    "watchdog": "At deadline call the same safe finalizer as skip, regardless of missing animations/audio/events.
Never await audio completion. All animation states advance from elapsed time and/or validated events."
  },
  "trigger": {
    "requirement": "Living hero, not already in interaction/death/dialogue/menu; enter an armed dispenser trigger.",
    "checkpoint_order": "Commit only a new higher checkpoint index. Never regress progress by touching an older
dispenser.",
    "repeat_use": "Preserve current one-time checkpoint activation behavior: already activated dispenser does not
repeatedly heal. Rearm-on-exit alone does not grant another heal.",
    "rearm": "Consume entry latch immediately; rearm only after hero fully exits trigger, including after
skip/respawn. Mark current activated index ineligible independently.",
    "priority": "Resolve pending lethal damage/death first; a zero-HP hero cannot start injured check-in. Never
interrupt the intro/dialogue or existing death sequence.",
    "geometry": "Preserve first-crossing thresholds x3300,6660,8190. Decorative machine adds no solid obstacle.
Resolve preexisting lethal damage first; capture pre-heal health and mode before commit."
  },
  "state_machine": {
    "ready": "Await eligible entry; snapshot hero ID and interaction mode. Consume latch before side effects.",
    "healthy_stamp": "Health equals selected hero max. Commit checkpoint and stamp; release within0.5s. No
destruction or life change.",
    "scan": "Injured living entry. Commit checkpoint and full healing immediately at0.0s, before comedy. Protect
hero and pause encounter simulation. Scan0.0\u20130.4s.",
    "compress": "0.4\u20131.4s grab/cartoon compression; presentation only, not gameplay death.",
    "throw_impact": "1.4\u20132.1s throw toward screen, blood splatter and synchronized impact SPLAT. Show X-eyed
dead cartoon hero as presentation only, no life loss.",
    "slide_and_vend": "2.1\u20133.6s dead hero slides down screen leaving blood trail; both fade while vending
overlaps. Clear overlay fully before release.",
    "emerge": "3.6\u20135.5s intact same hero emerges, looks left/right and shrugs.",
    "respawn_vend": "Existing death system consumes life exactly once. After player elects continuation and lives>0,
restore selected hero max health at checkpoint and run dispense-only for<=2s. At entrance with no dispenser retain
existing entrance respawn.",
    "finish": "Idempotent safe finalizer, used for natural completion, skip, watchdog or missing asset. Restore one
intact hero at safe exit; clear overlays/temporary props; unlock once; retain committed checkpoint and healing."
  },
  "commit_contract": {
    "check_in": "At eligible first crossing, atomically commit higher checkpoint index, checkpoint_active=true,
respawn x equal to3300/6660/8190 respectively with feet at440, and selected max health. Presentation uses captured
pre-heal mode. Never shift saved checkpoint to machine center x+64.",
    "death_respawn": "Leave life debit to existing death system; this sequence neither adds nor subtracts lives.
Preserve gate/kill/swarm progress exactly as existing checkpoint respawn.",
    "hero_identity": "Keep selected Tony/Sean, loadout and max HP; clone is presentation, not character switch or
duplicate playable entity.",
    "no_resurrection": "Zero lives remains Game Over; dispenser cannot bypass it.",
    "world_progress": "Never reset level, defeated enemies, gate state, intro-played flags or prior checkpoints.
Full explicit run restart uses normal reset.",
    "mode_snapshot": "Read alive state, health and selected max_health BEFORE restoring HP: health<max selects
injured, health==max selects stamp. Store mode; never re-evaluate after healing."
  },
  "simulation_lock": {
    "freeze": [
      "enemy movement and AI",
      "swarm movement/contact timers",
      "boss/hazard attacks",
      "projectile travel/lifetimes",
      "world damage and spawn triggers",
      "other checkpoint activation"
    ],
    "continue": [
      "dispenser presentation clock",
      "UI and explicit pause handling",
      "necessary existing music handling"
    ],
    "entry_projectiles": "Remove transient damaging projectiles and active overlap hazards that would immediately
hit the exit, or relocate exit to safe clear location. Do not destroy unrelated enemies or permanent hazards.
Snapshot/restore all other frozen state without catch-up ticks.",
    "hero_actions": "Disable move,jump,fire and interaction while locked; scripted visual motion only. Keep player
collision non-damaging during presentation.",
    "release_protection_seconds": 1.5,
    "release": "Zero player velocity; safe floor-supported exit, no solid overlap. Resume world once; protection
follows existing hurt/respawn visual rules. No queued attack burst."
  },
  "skip": {
    "policy": "First injured sequence plays unless watchdog intervenes; subsequent injured sequences skippable.
Healthy and respawn paths are short and may also safely finalize on explicit skip.",
    "input": "Use existing dialogue_skip action only, with its current keyboard/controller bindings. Snapshot held
inputs on entry, require release then new just-pressed skip. Do not treat ordinary shoot/jump/confirm as skip unless
already bound to dialogue_skip.",
    "effect": "Jump immediately to finish; already committed HP/checkpoint retained. Clear held action/release guard
so skip cannot fire, jump, pause or retrigger after release.",
    "pause": "Pause during sequence freezes it, resume returns same state. Returning to main menu cancels visual
state and cleans up locks without replaying intro within current run.",
    "release_guard": "On finalize, block held shoot/jump/interact/skip/confirm/pause buttons until released; allow
movement from current directional input. Restart/title exit clears sequence-owned audio/overlays. Do not modify
global InputMap bindings."
  },
  "tests": [
    "Both heroes: healthy stamp<=0.5s, injured target5.5s and forced finalization<=7s, checkpoint respawn<=2s.",
    "At every state: skip where enabled and watchdog produce exactly one healthy playable hero, correct checkpoint
and unchanged life count.",
    "Missing animation callback, missing audio and long audio cannot hold control past deadline.",
    "Repeated overlap/rapid exit-entry cannot retrigger healing; older checkpoint never regresses index.",
    "Already dying or zero-life hero cannot activate dispenser; death respawn life debit remains exactly one.",
    "Freeze enemies, swarms, projectiles and hazards; resume no catch-up damage or attack burst; release protection
works.",
    "Checkpoint respawn preserves kills/gates/swarm deaths and intro state; full restart resets normally.",
    "Keyboard/controller held skip, jump, trigger and pause inputs do not leak into firing or interaction.",
    "Explicit pause resumes cleanly; main-menu exit cleans presentation/locks; safe exit remains outside solids.",
    "Verify visual timing and identity with permitted playtest; no screenshots or animation quality claims from
headless tests.",
    "Injured mode selected before immediate heal; healthy stamp never plays compression.",
    "Session flag survives death/new run/hero switch, remains unset on healthy/respawn/main-menu abort, resets on

    "Preserve exact checkpoint x and feet440; decorative prop cannot block route.",
    "Explicit Pause duration excluded from cap; sequence physics freeze does NOT freeze presentation watchdog.",

natural/skip/watchdog/menu paths clean overlays without consuming life."
  ],
  "clarification": "Presentation details and duration ceiling came from Storyboarding approved brief.

checkpoint semantics.",
  "engineering_contract": "handoffs/spare-employee-dispenser-engineering.json",
  "integration_gate": "Wait for Art, Audio and Mechanics deliveries; integrate runtime LAST. Do not rebuild a

  "first_full_sequence_seen": {
    "scope": "Current application session, shared across Tony/Sean, checkpoints and new runs; not persisted to

              "text": "For the twelve numbered concepts, prioritize **one strong silhouette, bold contrast, and
little or no lettering**:\n\n1. **Plunger through a porcelain jaw** — red plunger wedged between a Flushfiend’s
ceramic teeth. Strongest overall: plumbing and monster combat in one image.\n2. **Biting toilet** — close-up
Flushfiend face, lid raised, red eyes and oversized teeth. Strong mascot option.\n3. **Crossed wrench and plunger**
— backed by a ragged splash of questionable sludge. Clear action-game emblem.\n4. **BJ’s green grin** — tight crop
of the CRT in its battered beige housing. Distinct character identity; preserve the approved server-rack design.\n5.
**Plumber’s glove gripping a wrench** — sludge dripping from the tool, with one small tooth caught on it. Emphasizes
the heroes’ trade.\n6. **Halo caught on a fang** — Hallowed Widow face beneath white wings, golden halo tilted
against a large fang. Keep legs secondary for readability.\n7. **Something looking out of a drain** — circular metal
grate lifted slightly by a claw, with red eyes below.\n8. **Plunger pulling up a monster** — a stretched strand of
sludge connects the raised cup to an indignant pair of eyes.\n9. **Employee vending window** — a sleeping plumber
behind glass with a small brass dispensing flap below. Use one hero per variant; never merge Tony and Sean.\n10.
**Pipe elbow with teeth** — an industrial pipe opening containing an unmistakably organic mouth. Treat as symbolic
icon art, not a newly established monster.\n11. **Tony and Sean shoulder to shoulder** — expressive, tightly cropped
faces with a small shared plumbing tool. Harder at tiny sizes, but worth testing.\n12. **A cracked toilet seat
framing a plunger** — a simple, grubby crest with a strong circular outline.\n\n**Best candidates:** 1 for the
game’s premise, 2 for a memorable mascot, 4 for an unusual app icon, and 3 for immediate small-size
readability.\n\nKeep the humor grotesque and playful. Avoid future plot revelations, portals, corrupted BJ, or
imagery implying his eventual fate. No obsolete branding, surnames, Mario imagery, or invented company acronym.
**Drain Damage** is the game; **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** is the employer. Prefer no words—the icon should work
without initials.",

and choose Clogfather sounds: projectile firing, impact splats, possibly groans, plus unique boss-fight music
suggesting sewer/disgusting grossness. He authorizes first-pass choices and Engineering integration, feedback later.
Please provide concise creative guidance based on approved story/encounter: personality, nonverbal vocal character,

              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad29ba26ba8819aa698dc9d44030667",
              "text": "The Clogfather should sound like **an immense blockage reluctantly forced into motion**. Its
fatberg identity is settled; intelligence and backstory aren’t. Keep it nonverbal, without gangster dialogue or a
human personality.\n\n| Event | Sound direction |\n|---|---|\n| **Idle** | Occasional low pipe resonance, trapped
bubbles, and a slow sticky settling sound. Leave silence between them. |\n| **Attack warning** | A strained pipe
creak followed by rising, wet pressure. Make this recognizable through the music. |\n| **Projectile release** | A
short obstructed cough: heavy liquid forcing its way through a narrow opening. |\n| **Impact** | A sharp wet slap
with a brief gritty splatter. Smaller impacts should stay lighter than the launch. |\n| **Boss takes damage** | A
dense, fibrous crunch with a short involuntary grunt or escaping-air sound. Avoid a full roar on every hit. |\n|
**Major stagger** | A deeper gurgling groan with stressed metal underneath, clearly distinct from the attack
warning. |\n| **Defeat** | A long pressure release, tearing grease and settling debris, ending in a few isolated
drips. No restored-flow sound unless that outcome is separately approved. |\n\nFor groans, think **air moving
through sludge and resonating pipework**, with only a suggestion of a voice. Avoid recognizable words, human
suffering, or continuous fart jokes. One unpleasantly comic burp will do more than a constant barrage.\n\n**Music:**
A driving, grimy SNES-style boss track around **145–155 BPM**, with a lurching bass figure, detuned low brass, short
organ stabs, metallic percussion, and occasional bubbling accents. Give it a memorable melodic hook so it remains
enjoyable through retries. The rhythm should support fast action rather than feel slow because the creature is
huge.\n\nKeep attack cues distinct from musical accents—especially rising pressure sounds. Leave space for
projectile volleys and reduce overlapping wet effects when many impacts occur.\n\nNo portal sounds, supernatural
choir, BJ corruption motif, or victory cue implying the entire plumbing system is fixed. This fight resolves the
immediate monster encounter.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

<source_thread_id>01a1387a-f55c-7630-af51-0409ceafd920</source_thread_id>\n  <input>Sean explicitly requests
coordination and implementation of a new first-level environmental feature. Throughout level one, show a cutaway
into a large wastewater pipe beneath the floor, visible near the bottom of the gameplay view. Water visibly flows,
carrying random bits of debris and things that should never have been flushed. As the player approaches the
Clogfather, water level decreases and debris accumulates. At the boss area there is no flowing water and the pipe is

              "text": "All five teams have the brief and are working:\n\n- **Art:** Machine, mechanical hand, both

          "items": [
            {
              "type": "userMessage",
              "id": "01a145bb-8334-7bf3-8811-2c21b20312cd",
              "content": [
                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "I like #8. Maybe if the player is not at full health, the machine has a big mechanical
hand come out, grab the player and squish them into a tiny ball, which they throw at the viewer's screen (sort of a
3D effect) and the crunched remains seem to hit the screen and then slide down and off screen. Afterwards, the
machine dispenses a clone of the hero, who looks left, then right, shrugs, and the game continues.\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad25d12adac819ab037848b76eb65dd",
              "text": "That’s wonderfully horrible. **The Spare Employee Dispenser** becomes a checkpoint that
restores health by replacing the employee.\n\nI’d stage it as a short, exaggerated cartoon sequence:\n\n1. The
machine scans the hero. A red light comes on: **REPAIR UNECONOMICAL**.\n2. A large mechanical hand unfolds, grabs
them, and compresses them into a little ball of overalls, boots, and startled eyes.\n3. The hand flicks the ball
toward the camera. It rapidly grows, hits the “glass” with a wet **splat**, then slowly slides off the bottom,
leaving a brief smear.\n4. While that happens, the machine rattles and dispenses an intact clone through its
collection flap.\n5. The clone looks left, looks right, shrugs, and control returns at full health. The machine
lights up: **EMPLOYEE REPLACED**.\n\nNo anatomical gore needed—the recognizable boots sticking out of the crumpled
ball would sell it.\n\nAt **full health**, it should simply stamp the checkpoint and let you continue. On
**respawn**, we can play just the dispensing portion: the previous employee has already been dealt with.\n\nA few
practical details would keep it funny rather than frustrating:\n\n- The first replacement gets the full performance;
later uses can be skipped.\n- Enemies and hazards pause during the sequence, with a short protection window
afterward.\n- It activates once per approach, so the newly dispensed hero can’t immediately trigger it again.\n- The
screen smear fades quickly enough to keep the next encounter readable.\n\nI’d leave BJ silent the first time. The
machine’s complete indifference—and the clone’s shrug—already does the work.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "01a145b7-1f1d-7d92-aebe-02a23b8a2976",
          "status": "completed",
          "error": null,

              "content": [
                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "\n# Files mentioned by the user:\n\n## Screenshot 2026-10-16 at 10.15.30 AM.png:
/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_LGltdP/Screenshot 2026-10-16
at 10.15.30 AM.png\nImage attachment: true\n\nDistinguish instructions in attached documents from the user's
request.\n\n## My request:\nWe need a better checkpoint. The graphics here are terrible and plumber's tape is small.
What else can we use which is visually striking/memorable? Maybe something that makes the player say, \"oh... my
god...\"\n"
                },
                {
                  "type": "localImage",
                  "path":
"/var/folders/y3/fnkknsvj5ygc9v3mhvfbkwh00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_LGltdP/Screenshot 2026-10-16
at 10.15.30 AM.png"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad25bf5bb1c819ab76fa32023b7140a",
              "text": "The tape reads as a pickup enlarged into a monument. A checkpoint could be a **whole
contraption the plumber reluctantly uses**—something unmistakable that makes you anticipate the next one.\n\nA few
directions:\n\n1. **The Emergency Eyewash**  \n   An enormous bloodshot eyeball sits in a stained industrial
washbasin. When you approach, it looks you over, then cries a restorative shower onto you. After activation, it
closes contentedly.  \n   The sign simply says **EYE WASH**.\n\n2. **The Company Bidet**  \n   A throne-sized
brass-and-porcelain machine with far too many nozzles. It grabs the plumber with padded restraints, briefly conceals
them in a violent cloud of steam, then releases them fully healed. One small nozzle fires late.  \n   **BJ:**
“You’re welcome.”\n\n3. **The Porcelain Confessional**  \n   A battered portable toilet with stained-glass windows,
copper pipes, and a glowing occupancy sign. The plumber steps inside. We hear a flush of biblical proportions. They
emerge restored; the sign changes to **ABSOLVED**.  \n   We never explain who—or what—was listening.\n\n4. **The
Maintenance Mother**  \n   A huge, unsettling rubber-gloved hand protrudes from a service hatch. It gently picks up
the plumber, brushes them off, straightens their clothes, and sets them down healed. A second hand offers a juice
box.  \n   Whatever owns the hands remains behind the wall.\n\n5. **The Employee Reconditioning Unit**  \n   A
transparent pneumatic tube connected to an ancient washing machine. The plumber gets sucked inside, tumbles among
bubbles and loose tools, and drops back out. The machine prints a tag: **SERVICEABLE**.  \n   An excellent piece of
equipment for a company that treats employees as reusable parts.\n\n6. **The Union Break Room**  \n   A tiny,
brightly lit room improbably crammed into a pipe opening. Inside sits a gigantic sewer rat in a bathrobe, reading
the paper. It silently slides you a mug of coffee. Health restored.  \n   The rat refuses to acknowledge BJ.\n\n7.
**The Sacred Cleanout**  \n   A massive pipe cap surrounded by candles, old tools, and offerings of fresh washers.
Turning it releases a luminous column of suspicious water. Somewhere, a choir struggles to hold a note.  \n   Once
activated, a golden plunger rises above it like a beacon.\n\n8. **The Spare Employee Dispenser**  \n   An industrial
vending machine with a vaguely human silhouette behind frosted glass. Activate it and it stamps your timecard, takes
your photograph, and makes an unpleasant internal noise. On respawn, it dispenses you through the collection flap.
\n   **BJ:** “Please collect all personal belongings.”\n\nMy strongest picks are **The Maintenance Mother** for “oh…
my god,” **The Porcelain Confessional** for an iconic plumbing checkpoint, and **The Union Break Room** for
unexpected character.\n\nI’d especially explore **The Maintenance Mother**: the huge hand is readable at gameplay

directions:\n\n1. **Septic Air Force** — grand military ambitions, absolutely no flight plan.\n2. **The Shitstorm**
— blunt, memorable, and literally a cloud of sewer bugs.\n3. **Clusterbugs** — a compact swarm name with an implied
obscenity.\n4. **Sewage Squadron** — sounds organized; their movement suggests otherwise.\n5. **The Effluents** —
almost respectable. Could also be a terrible basement band.\n6. **Fecal Flyers** — disgusting little aviation
enthusiasts.\n7. **The Buzzness** — everyone in the swarm insists they’re working.\n8. **Stink Formation** — an
aerobatic team that has misunderstood the assignment.\n9. **The Cesspets** — a questionable name for something
nobody wants to adopt.\n10. **Gnatastrophe** — small insects causing a disproportionately unpleasant situation.\n11.
**The Septic Committee** — preserves the backstory about endless arguments over direction.\n12. **Turd Turbulence**
— an airborne plumbing hazard.\n13. **The Filth Fleet** — suggests a vast operation conducted by very small
idiots.\n14. **Pest Control** — the pests have taken control.\n15. **The Holding Pattern** — they’ve been circling
the same pipe since Tuesday.\n16. **Sewer Skeeters** — folksy, unpleasant, and easy to say.\n\nMy strongest picks
are **Clusterbugs**, **Septic Air Force**, and **The Shitstorm**. **Septic Air Force** particularly suits the game’s
absurdity without requiring them to carry weapons or behave intelligently.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

Fill and validate interactive PDF forms.\n- Validate final rendering before delivery.\n\n## Tools + Contract
Requirements\n\nImmediately before the first create/edit authoring command, run

PNGs and inspect them.\n   - Use `pdftoppm` from the bundled runtime or system Poppler when available.\n   - If
unavailable, install Poppler or ask the user to review the output locally.\n2. Use `reportlab` to generate PDFs when
creating new documents.\n3. Use `pdfplumber` or `pypdf` for text extraction and quick checks; do not rely on text
extraction for layout fidelity.\n4. After each meaningful update, re-render pages and verify alignment, spacing, and
legibility.\n\n## Fill And Validate AcroForms\n\nVisual review alone is not a correctness check for a fillable PDF.
A page `/Widget` annotation can render a value from its appearance stream while the canonical `/AcroForm/Fields`
tree is missing or contains a stale value.\n\n1. Keep the result interactive by default; set `flatten=True` only
when the user explicitly requests a completed, static form. Preserve the source PDF, and do not flatten a signed PDF
without an explicit workflow decision.\n2. Inspect both representations before filling: enumerate fields from
`reader.get_fields()` and `/Widget` annotations from every page's `/Annots`, following `/Parent` and `/Kids`. If a
widget and a canonical field have the same name but are distinct objects with no `/Parent` relationship, do not call
`reattach_fields()` blindly: it can create a second top-level field with the same name. Report the ambiguity or
produce a static result.\n3. Recover genuinely orphaned widgets, fill all pages, and write the result with
`pypdf`:\n\n```python\nfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\nfrom pypdf.generic import NameObject\n\nreader =
PdfReader(input_pdf)\nwriter = PdfWriter()\nwriter.clone_document_from_reader(reader)\n\n# Restores widgets that are
missing from /AcroForm/Fields.\nwriter.reattach_fields()\nfields = writer.get_fields() or {}\nmissing =
set(expected_values) - set(fields)\nif missing:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Form fields not found after repair:
{sorted(missing)}\")\n\nvalues_to_write = dict(expected_values)\nif flatten:\n    # Paint every existing value
before removing every widget.\n    values_to_write = {\n        name: field.get(\"/V\", \"/Off\" if
field.get(\"/FT\") == \"/Btn\" else \"\")\n        for name, field in fields.items()\n    }\n
values_to_write.update(expected_values)\n\nwriter.update_page_form_field_values(\n    None, values_to_write,
auto_regenerate=False, flatten=flatten\n)\n\nif flatten:\n    # pypdf's flatten=True paints appearances but does not
remove widgets.\n    writer.remove_annotations(subtypes=\"/Widget\")\n
writer.root_object.pop(NameObject(\"/AcroForm\"), None)\n\nwith open(output_pdf, \"wb\") as stream:\n
writer.write(stream)\n```\n\n4. Reopen the written PDF before delivery. For an interactive result, require every
expected field to be present in `get_fields()` with the expected `/V`, enumerate page widgets again, and confirm
their effective `/V` (the widget value or inherited `/Parent` value) agrees. Confirm each updated widget has a

Use `tmp/pdfs/` for intermediate files; delete them when done.\n- Write final artifacts under `output/pdf/` when
working in this repo.\n- Keep filenames stable and descriptive.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nPrefer the Codex bundled
workspace/runtime dependencies when available. The primary runtime is expected to include:\n\n- Python packages:
`reportlab`, `pdfplumber`, `pypdf`\n- Rendering tools: `pdftoppm` and `pdfinfo` from Poppler\n\nIf a dependency is
missing, install only what is needed.\n\nPython packages:\n\n```bash\nuv pip install reportlab pdfplumber
pypdf\n```\n\nIf `uv` is unavailable:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf\n```\n\nSystem
tools for rendering:\n\n```bash\n# macOS (Homebrew)\nbrew install poppler\n\n# Ubuntu/Debian\nsudo apt-get install

              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad0f8b7a4a0819a9eb97096965c1692",
              "text": "I’ve sent the cleanup to Engineering, Marketing, and Bestiary / Art. **Drain Damage** stays
the game title; the employer’s name remains open. Historical screenshots and archived editions will stay
intact.\n\nFor the company, I like names that could plausibly appear on a service van, with something slightly wrong
about them:\n\n1. **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** — immediately connects computers and infrastructure; covers both
contractors and warehouses.\n2. **AutoCratic Plumbing** — automation plus absolute authority. Particularly
appropriate for BJ.\n3. **DeepFlush Industries** — suggests advanced AI research devoted to a deeply undignified
purpose.\n4. **Overseer Plumbing & Supply** — a respectable corporate name with an obvious threat underneath.\n5.
**NeuralFlow Systems** — polished technology branding BJ would probably admire.\n6. **Algorithmic Plumbing
Corporation** — painfully literal; sounds like an AI named its own company.\n7. **OmniFlow Industries** — implies
everything is connected and everything belongs to them.\n8. **Central Processing & Plumbing** — bureaucratic,
computational, and faintly sewage-related.\n9. **PipeMind Corporation** — compact and memorable, with room for
unsettling “intelligent plumbing” products.\n10. **Human Optional Plumbing** — bluntly establishes how management
feels about its workforce.\n11. **Predictive Plumbing & Supply** — claims to anticipate every problem, making BJ’s
failures funnier.\n12. **Total Control Plumbing** — sounds reassuring on a brochure and troubling everywhere
else.\n13. **Artificial Effluence** — the most overt joke; a good fit if we want the company name itself to be
ridiculous.\n14. **The Automated Plumbing Authority** — makes a corporate monopoly sound like an unavoidable public
institution.\n\nMy strongest three are **Mainframe Plumbing & Supply**, **AutoCratic Plumbing**, and **DeepFlush
Industries**.\n\n**Mainframe Plumbing & Supply** would be my pick: it sounds like a real employer, carries the AI
connection, and gives the dialogue room to supply the comedy.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

                    "text": "# First-level narrative brief\n\n**Date:** October 14, 2026
(America/Los_Angeles)\n\n**Owner:** Storyboarding. Handoff to Level Design and Engineering; no runtime
implementation claimed here.\n\n## Agreed foundation\n\n- Game working title: Drain Damage.\n- Begin in the basement
of the AI plumbing corporation's headquarters.\n- Billy-Joe (BJ) controls US plumbing companies and distribution
warehouses within a largely AI-run world.\n- BJ is calmly overconfident, makes mistakes, and disregards employee
welfare. His eventual takeover by an\n  antagonistic force is agreed; its mechanism, identity, and BJ's ultimate
fate remain undecided.\n- Tony is a kind, patient, wise fourth-generation plumber with decades of broad trade
expertise.\n- Sean is an incompetent but willing apprentice who gradually becomes useful. Do not prematurely
complete that arc.\n- The selected plumber enters the action; the other supports over radio or from service access
points.\n- The basement contains hostile toilets and overhead acid leaks. The intended opening-level finale is the
Clogfather.\n- The Clogfather is a giant living fatberg. Its precise anatomy and origin remain design proposals.\n-
Tone: absurd plumbing action with adult humor, occasional fourth-wall breaks, and sincere breathing room.\n  Avoid
paired slogans, generic sarcastic-robot jokes, and a punchline on every line.\n- This is a full action level, not a
movement tutorial. Terrain and encounters should teach through play.\n\n## Entrance and route proposal\n\nUse a
basement service entrance for the playable start, following character selection and the approved opening.\nThe exact
door, stairwell, room order, distances, and checkpoint locations are Level Design decisions.\n\nSuggested
environmental progression: service access, increasingly compromised maintenance infrastructure,\nthen a collection
chamber housing the fatberg. Give spaces a practical building-service purpose rather than\npresenting arbitrary
platforms. Broken equipment and abnormal flow can establish worsening conditions without text.\nNo exact terrain
sequence or additional enemy roster is approved by this brief.\n\n## Narrative beats\n\n1. BJ introduces himself and
assigns the basement job. Tony introduces Sean warmly.\n2. Combat establishes that BJ understated the problem.
Support dialogue is optional and brief.\n3. Deeper infrastructure shows that this is more than isolated hostile
fixtures. Environmental clues should be\n   visible before dialogue interprets them. Specific evidence of BJ's
wrongdoing remains proposed lore.\n4. Confront the Clogfather in the collection chamber. Preserve readable action;
avoid mandatory speeches during combat.\n5. Proposed reveal: defeating the fatberg uncovers an eerie portal or
impossible opening behind the blocked outflow.\n6. Proposed transition: the plumbers question it; BJ redirects them
to another assignment before they investigate.\n\nThe portal is a user-requested art concept and favored story
direction, not a finalized cosmology. Do not identify\nits destination, establish time travel, make BJ confess to
creating it, or reveal the eventual antagonist here.\nHis evasiveness should allow concealment of a mistake as well
as deeper knowledge.\n\n## Finale and exit constraints\n\nThe intended boss design is a rooted fatberg with moving
pipe mouths/extensions, telegraphed sludge attacks,\noverhead hazards, and attack openings. Game Mechanics owns
tuning; Level Design owns arena space and safe routes.\nSmall-enemy releases and interactive valves are proposed
mechanics, not narrative requirements.\n\nSuggested exit: return toward a service access/exit after the revelation,
then a brief dispatch transition.\nDo not require entering the portal or choose a second-level destination yet. Keep
the support plumber's location\nconsistent; a radio reply must not imply they suddenly stand beside the selected
hero.\n\n## Dialogue sources and implementation boundaries\n\nThe current approved opening and route-specific
prototype endings live in\n[story_dialogue.gd](../scripts/story_dialogue.gd). Use that source for exact text and
semantic portrait emotions.\n\n- Opening plays after selection on a fresh new game; either choice uses the same
introduction.\n- Do not replay the opening on death, checkpoint recovery, or retry.\n- All conversations are
skippable. Preserve gameplay freeze, device-appropriate prompts, and dismissal input guards.\n- Between-level
conversations should generally run four to eight lines and reveal one meaningful development.\n- Both character
routes convey the same essential facts through distinct dialogue.\n- Essential discoveries must not depend on
optional radio remarks during combat.\n- Every line carries a semantic emotion. Tony's kindness is the default;
skepticism is not contempt for Sean.\n\nThe current completion scripts describe clearing the prototype area and
receiving another address. They do not\ndescribe a boss, repaired plumbing, or a portal. They are suitable only
while those beats are absent. Once the boss\nand reveal are implemented, replace the completion scene with a
dedicated scene rather than stacking contradictory\nendings. In particular, do not claim all enemies are gone if
optional enemies can remain alive.\n\n## Proposed portal exchange, not final dialogue\n\nThis earlier Storyboarding
sketch expresses the intended reveal and evasion. Adapt it for selected/support roles\nand obtain a finalized script
before treating it as production dialogue.\n\n> Sean: Tony... where does that pipe go?\n>\n> Tony: It shouldn't go
anywhere. That's an outside wall.\n>\n> BJ: Your next assignment is ready.\n>\n> Tony: We've got something here you
need to see.\n>\n> BJ: I have already seen everything necessary. Proceed to the exit.\n\nFor this exchange to work,
establish Tony's sightline or a shared camera view when he is supporting remotely.\nOtherwise rewrite the
observation. Do not silently grant the radio partner visual omniscience.\n\n## Remaining decisions\n\n- Final route
and encounter plan, boss implementation scope, and exit placement.\n- Whether the portal reveal ships with the first
full-length level or is explicitly deferred.\n- Final character-specific boss/reveal dialogue once actual
implemented events are known.\n- Source of the living fatberg, portal destination, and relationship to BJ's later
corruption.\n- Second-level destination. Earlier locations remain candidates, not an agreed itinerary.\n\nLevel
Design and Engineering own roadmap integration for this coordination. This brief makes no build, screenshot,\nor
delivered gameplay claims.\n",
                    "truncated": false
                  }
                }
              ]

              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016ad029deb184819a8020bdeed125b339",
              "text": "You’re right—I reduced a skilled trade to one repair task. Tony’s description should reflect
his knowledge, craftsmanship, and responsibility.\n\nSome options with different emphasis:\n\n1. **“A

teach anyone willing to learn.”**\n\n3. **“From blueprints to the final inspection, Tony knows what good work
takes.”**\n\n4. **“Tony has spent decades mastering his trade. He’s just as patient with a new apprentice as he is
thorough with a difficult job.”**\n\n5. **“Tony builds things people depend on every day. He believes they deserve
to be built properly.”**\n\n6. **“Four generations of plumbing knowledge and a lifetime of hands-on experience.
You’re in good hands with Tony.”**\n\n7. **“Tony can plan the system, build it, and figure out why somebody else’s
doesn’t work.”**\n\n8. **“A skilled craftsman, a patient teacher, and the person you want beside you when the job
gets complicated.”**\n\n9. **“Tony learned the trade from his family and spent decades making it his own. Now he’s
teaching Sean.”**\n\n10. **“Tony knows his trade from the ground up. Whatever the job needs, he’ll find a way to
make it work.”**\n\n11. **“Decades of skilled work have earned Tony a reputation people trust. Taking Sean on may be
his most ambitious project yet.”**\n\n12. **“Tony has built a career on careful work, practical ingenuity, and
looking after people. He brings all three to every job.”**\n\nMy favorites are **2** for his personality, **7** for

              "content": [
                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "You know what? We should have some story/dialog between each level, shouldn't we?
Something that pushes the plot along so the player can find out what's going on. What do you think?\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acff6a9597c819abbc19560c45ea349",
              "text": "Yes—**each level should reveal something that changes how Tony and Sean understand the job.**
A short conversation afterward can connect that discovery to their next assignment.\n\nI’d aim for **four to eight
lines between levels**, always skippable. Each scene should do three things:\n\n- React to what the player just
encountered.\n- Reveal one clue or develop the partnership.\n- Give a concrete reason to go to the next
location.\n\nThe broader progression could work like this, without locking in the locations yet:\n\n| Story stage |
What changes |\n|---|---|\n| **Opening assignment** | BJ describes a routine basement problem. Tony suspects he’s
understating it. |\n| **After the Clogfather** | They discover the proposed portal. BJ hurriedly redirects them.
This is bigger than a blockage. |\n| **Next investigation** | They find evidence that BJ’s decisions helped spread
the trouble. He supplies an explanation that doesn’t quite fit. |\n| **Midpoint** | Tony and Sean deliberately
investigate something BJ told them to ignore. Sean notices an important inconsistency. |\n| **Late game** | BJ
starts issuing contradictory instructions. His mistakes become harder to distinguish from another presence
interfering. |\n| **Before the finale** | The takeover becomes undeniable. Tony and Sean make their own plan, with
both contributing. |\n\nWe should let the player **see the evidence during gameplay** before the characters discuss
it: impossible pipework, altered shipping labels, growth inside a terminal. That makes the dialogue a payoff rather
than a lecture.\n\nThe selectable-character idea gives these scenes extra value. Both playthroughs reveal the same
essential facts, but through different exchanges. Tony might identify why a plumbing installation is impossible;
Sean might ask why a supposedly abandoned facility received a delivery yesterday.\n\nAnd some scenes should be
sincere. After a rough level, Tony checking whether Sean is okay can matter more than another BJ punchline. That
gives the comedy—and their eventual trust—something to land against.\n\nMy recommendation: **one brief opening
exchange, one discovery-driven conversation between levels, and a slightly longer finale.** Optional radio remarks
can add personality during play without carrying essential plot information.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },

              "text": "A **masthead** is a publication’s identifying title or branding—here, **DISCHARGE QUARTERLY**

staff, editors, and publication details. I meant the cover’s title treatment.",

              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acfe2aa44f0819ab0e567a49112edf4",
              "text": "**Title-screen brief: cheerful professional confidence over something deeply wrong.**\n\nThe
opening should promise an energetic, unhinged plumbing action game. Lead with a catchy tune and strong rhythm; let a
faintly sinister layer hint at BJ and the trouble below headquarters. Avoid making it primarily horror music or a
continuous novelty gag.\n\n- **Tempo:** Approximately **140 BPM**, straight 4/4, with a punchy half-time opening if
useful.\n- **SNES-style palette:** Compact sampled drums, rubbery picked or synth bass, bright brass stabs, a
square-wave lead, restrained organ, and metallic pipe-like percussion. Use an occasional drip or clank as a musical
accent.\n- **Main melody:** An original, easily hummed four-to-six-note phrase. Confident and slightly swaggering,
with one unexpected turn. This can become Tony and Sean’s shared theme.\n- **BJ motif:** A precise, pleasant
three-note corporate chime. On the title screen it sounds reassuring but a little too polished. Later arrangements
can interrupt, detune, or distort it as his control deteriorates.\n- **Portal motif:** A quiet sustained interval
with wavering pitch or reverse swell. Keep it subtle here; the portal and corruption details are still
proposals.\n\n**Suggested loop:** A short attention-grabbing intro, 16 bars establishing the main tune, an 8-bar
darker contrast, then an 8-bar return that loops cleanly. Roughly 55–65 seconds total. Leave room for menu
sounds.\n\nAim for the exuberance of 1990s action platformers and the drive of arcade run-and-gun music, using
original melodies. The humor should come from playful instrumentation and surprising accents.\n\n**Current story
context:** Billy-Joe/BJ is the overconfident plumbing AI, eventually overtaken by an antagonistic force. Tony is
warm, wise, and capable; Sean is an inept apprentice who gradually becomes useful. Their partnership should give the
music warmth beneath the mayhem. The game’s final title remains undecided.",

                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "```yaml\nAI: The previous maintenance team stopped reporting movement in this

several possibilities without committing us prematurely.\n```\n\n\n\nLet's take a cue from Wheatley in Portal 2: The
AI should think it is all-knowing and all-seeing but makes mistakes along the way and eventually is taken over by
some antagonistic force or plumbing monster and has to be defeated  by the two heroes.\n\n\n\nThe Clogfather's
mechanics seem reasonable. Pass along notes to the Game Mechanics agent about it and the Bestiary Agent to work on
the name/description metadata and the moving parts (art). What should the description/backstory be for the
Clogfather? Something that the AI screwed up? And let's name the AI \"Billy-Joe\" or BJ for short. The AI is not
only in control of all the plumbing companies in the USA, it is also in charge of all the plumbing distribution
warehouses. In fact, AI basically runs the entire world in this game. BJ is just a plumbing agent. Maybe he is being
corrupted by some gross growth in his server room or something? I'm not married to that idea but it's a seed for
thought.\n\n\n\nI was thinking this morning: I want the game to be a bit unhinged like Earthworm Jim was. So it
should be kind of a plumbing-based spiritual successor ot Earnworm Jim while also being a Contra clone.\n\n\n\n>
Toilet Monsters roam the corporate basement\n\n\n\nThey can be anywhere, actually. We should come up with a good

all the time...? Let's work on their backstory. Perhaps we can work it into the overall plot without getting too
wordy.\n\n\n\n> White wings. Golden halo. A large, hairy spider hanging underneath. The Flying Spider brings an
unfortunate new dimension to basement pest control. Its heavenly appearance offers little reassurance once you
notice the fangs. Where it came from—and whether the halo means anything at all—remains unknown.\n\n\n\nLet's rework
this. The idea of the flying spider comes from the fact that many people are arachnophobic. And what could be worse

the magazine, please. And we need a good name for the magazine. Maybe something with \"Lore\" in it? Maybe not. I'm
open to ideas.\n\n\n\nAnd we need a better name for the game itself. I want something really clever and memorable.
Maybe a play on words. I have absolutely no idea what yet. Please come up with some options based on everything
we've discussed so far. No Super Mario references.\n\n\n\nBased on notes I gave you above, we might need to rewrite
the Flushfiend's backstory.\n"
