              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acfe2446ad4819ab72a2dbb3c1ec116",
              "text": "Agreed about that AI line: it doesn’t answer Tony’s question coherently. A cleaner exchange
would be:\n\n> **BJ:** The previous maintenance team stopped responding in this area.  \n> **Tony:** Did they make
it out?  \n> **BJ:** Their replacements did arrive.  \n> **Tony:** That wasn’t what I asked.\n\nBJ understands the
question. He considers staffing continuity the relevant answer.\n\n**Billy-Joe gives us a strong story direction.**
He controls America’s plumbing companies and distribution warehouses within a world largely run by AI. He believes
his visibility is complete and his conclusions infallible. His mistakes accumulate, he conceals evidence, and
eventually something takes control of him. Tony and Sean must defeat the resulting threat. The invading force,
takeover mechanism, and whether BJ survives remain open.\n\nHis calm voice will be particularly effective as his
control slips. Early on, he confidently misidentifies a problem. Later, he insists a room is empty while something
enormous moves through it.\n\nThe Earthworm Jim/Contra direction also helps: grotesque, surprising enemies and
absurd situations, with fast, readable action. We can let the visuals do plenty of the comedy so the dialogue
doesn’t have to perform constantly.\n\n**Proposed plot connection**\n\nI’d connect the events this way, without
settling the entire mythology yet:\n\n1. BJ distributes intelligent plumbing fixtures nationwide. This explains why
Flushfiends can appear almost anywhere.\n2. His maintenance decisions allow the Clogfather to develop beneath
headquarters.\n3. Defeating it exposes an impossible opening hidden inside the blocked outflow.\n4. BJ redirects the
plumbers before they can investigate. At first, he could simply be covering up an embarrassing discovery.\n5. Later,
evidence suggests something is spreading through infrastructure BJ believes he controls.\n6. Eventually, it reaches
him.\n\nThe server-room growth is a promising visual for that last development: something wet and organic occupying
a place BJ considers clean, controlled, and entirely his. I’d keep it provisional until we choose the final
antagonist.\n\nThe portal reveal could be brief:\n\n> **Sean:** Tony… where does that pipe go?  \n> **Tony:** It
shouldn’t go anywhere. That’s an outside wall.  \n> **BJ:** Your next assignment is ready.  \n> **Tony:** We’ve got
something here you need to see.  \n> **BJ:** I have already seen everything necessary. Proceed to the
exit.\n\n**Revised monster lore — drafts**\n\n**Flushfiend**\n\n> Billy-Joe wanted a toilet that could think for
itself. Through his distribution warehouses, he shipped networked smart fixtures across the country, then upgraded
them with artificial intelligence. They learned quickly. Unfortunately, their first shared conclusion concerned what
humans kept doing to them. Now Flushfiends stalk bathrooms, businesses, and anywhere else the rollout reached. BJ
calls it a customer-relations issue. The toilets have stopped accepting feedback.\n\nThis gives them a simple,
memorable grievance. Their rebellion can begin independently of the dimensional threat; we don’t need every bizarre
creature to have the same origin.\n\n**The Hallowed Widow**\n\n> For years, the worst thing about a basement spider
was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs,
white feathers, and a golden halo—every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the
floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Tony would very
much like them put back.\n\nAnd this is now **Tony’s** line:\n\n> “I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when
they died.”\n\nHis arachnophobia gives our otherwise reassuring expert something that genuinely rattles him. He
still helps Sean; he just strongly prefers helping from farther away.\n\n**The Clogfather — fatberg form locked in;
history proposed**\n\n> Billy-Joe classified repeated blockage warnings as duplicate reports and canceled the
cleaning crews. Beneath headquarters, grease hardened around wipes, roots, and a buried outflow until the blockage
filled the chamber. Then it began moving against the current. The Clogfather grew around something BJ’s diagrams do
not show. Removing it will restore access—but what it has been hiding may be worse than the clog.\n\nThis makes BJ
responsible for letting the blockage grow without prematurely declaring that he created the portal or knowingly
summoned anything.\n\n**Game-name candidates**\n\nThese are creative candidates; availability hasn’t been
checked.\n\n| Name | Why it fits |\n|---|---|\n| **Waste of Humanity** | My strongest overall pick. Sewage, hostile
AI, and humanity’s predicament in three words. |\n| **Pipe Dreams & Lead Nightmares** | Plumbing absurdity meets
gunfire. Strong 1990s box-art energy. |\n| **Drain Damage** | Short, punchy, and suitably unhinged. |\n| **Clog &
Loaded** | Immediately communicates plumbing plus shooting. |\n| **Plumb Crazy** | Tradesman wordplay that captures
the tone. |\n| **Backflow: Everything Comes Up** | Works with the uprising, monsters, and dimensional intrusion.
|\n| **Shit Outta Luck** | Strong adult-comedy identity, though it emphasizes crudeness more than the larger
premise. |\n| **Plumbageddon** | Compact, ridiculous, and easy to imagine across a title screen. |\n\nMy shortlist
is **Waste of Humanity**, **Drain Damage**, and **Clog & Loaded**. Of those, *Waste of Humanity* gives us the most
room to build a distinctive world.\n\n**Magazine-name candidates**\n\n- **Unclogged** — my favorite; subtitle:
*Monsters, Myths & Maintenance*.\n- **Pipe Lore** — direct, compact, and specifically tied to the world.\n- **Lore
from Below** — more eerie, especially once the portal enters the story.\n- **The Backflow** — sounds like an
irreverent trade publication.\n- **Grime & Lore** — a good fit for illustrated monster histories.\n\n**The handoffs
are sent and all three chats are working:** Game Mechanics has the Clogfather encounter notes; Bestiary / Art has
the metadata, moving boss parts, and animated eerie portal request; Marketing has the revised draft lore and Tony’s
quote for the magazine. The artwork and revised PDF are still in progress.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        }

              "text": "**Flushfiend — draft lore, proposed history**\n\nThe first Flushfiend report was filed as a
loose toilet mounting. The second mentioned bite marks. By the third, basement maintenance staff had started
knocking before entering empty bathrooms. Early sightings clustered around disused washrooms and backed-up service
lines beneath headquarters, although nobody has established whether the creatures originated there or simply found
the conditions agreeable. The surviving paperwork offers one consistent detail: tightening the bolts does not
resolve the issue, and puts your hands far too close to its mouth.\n\n**The Hallowed Widow — draft lore, proposed
history**\n\nMaintenance crews first noticed white feathers caught in the basement ventilation grilles. They
suspected pigeons until someone looked up and saw eight legs folding around a ceiling pipe. Stories of a haloed
spider soon spread between shifts, acquiring increasingly unreliable claims about blessings, omens, and unpaid
overtime. The name “Hallowed Widow” stuck after a worker described it as “something you’d pray to leave.” No
evidence connects it to an actual afterlife. Its wings and halo remain unexplained, despite several strongly worded
requests for clarification.",

                "text": "# Global coding standards\n\nRead the sections relevant to the task before editing or
reviewing that file type. These defaults supplement\n`AGENTS.md`; explicit user requests and applicable project
conventions take precedence. Tool-specific guidance\napplies when that tool is used, not as a requirement to add it
to every project.\n\n## General engineering and file hygiene\n\n- Read existing code and configuration first. Reuse
established helpers and command entry points before adding tools.\n- Keep changes scoped to the requested behavior.
Avoid speculative abstractions, unrelated cleanup, and comments or\n  annotations added to untouched code. Comment
why a non-obvious decision exists rather than restating the code.\n- Keep utilities cohesive, generic, and
dependency-light. Preserve established package/import boundaries. Add public\n  re-exports only intentionally;
internal helpers need not become public APIs.\n- Use named constants or enums for meaningful identifiers, opcodes,
and status values instead of unexplained literals.\n- Text files have no trailing whitespace, truly empty blank
lines, and exactly one final newline. Preserve required\n  format semantics and existing encoding/line endings. New
text defaults to UTF-8.\n- Default to a 120-character maximum for Python, Markdown, and shell, including comments
and banners. Wrap logically,\n  without routinely wrapping at 80. Do not split a literal or machine-readable value
in a way that changes its meaning.\n- Follow existing language/format settings for other files. Preserve user
changes and keep temporary artifacts in an\n  ignored scratch location, preferably the project's existing one. Do
not add scratch output to source trees or commits.\n- Read complete relevant tool output. Recover from errors or
truncation with a focused read, structured output, or a\n  suitable retry before drawing conclusions. Report
unresolved gaps; do not present partial results as complete.\n- Use fictional, neutral examples for reusable code
and documentation. Keep proprietary implementations, private names,\n  internal URLs, credentials, and
business-specific behavior out of cross-project material.\n\n## Python\n\n### Formatting, typing, and imports\n\n-
Use four-space code indentation and a **120-character** limit. Keep formatter/linter widths consistent when setting
up\n  a new project; use an existing project's declared settings when different.\n- Type function parameters, return
values, methods, and class attributes. Aim for strict type-checking quality; avoid\n  bypassing checks with
unexplained `Any`, ignores, or casts. Honor deliberate project exemptions such as test fixtures.\n- Prefer
`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, and `X | None` when supported by the project's Python version. Use postponed\n
annotations when the existing code or version compatibility calls for them.\n- Group imports standard library,
third-party, then local, with blank lines between groups. Use the configured\n  Ruff/isort rules rather than
manually fighting the sorter.\n- Preserve the supported Python version and package layout. Use the existing
environment and lockfile; when the project\n  uses Poetry, run tools through that environment. Ship typing metadata
when maintaining a typed library that uses it.\n\n### Docstrings and command-line tools\n\n- Document public APIs
and complex behavior. Match the package's established convention: Google-style sections where\n  configured, or
reST/Sphinx fields such as `:param:` and `:return:` where established. Do not mix or convert styles\n
opportunistically. For a new Python project without a preference, use Google-style docstrings consistently.\n- Keep
indentation inside docstrings in multiples of two spaces; prefer four-space list continuations over three-space\n
hanging alignment. Explain important exceptions, side effects, and constraints without duplicating obvious types.\n-
Prefer Click for new CLIs when already available or an appropriate dependency choice. Preserve existing CLI
frameworks\n  and avoid adding a dependency for a trivial script. With Click, use decorators, `click.echo()`, option
`envvar`\n  support,\n  and `context_settings={\"max_content_width\": 120}`. Keep help informative and consistent
with actual behavior.\n\n### Async, models, and generated artifacts\n\n- In an async codebase, keep I/O asynchronous
and avoid blocking the event loop. Keep sync/async bridges at deliberate\n  boundaries; do not scatter
`asyncio.run()` inside library code.\n- When Pydantic v2 is already the model layer, prefer immutable models and
`extra=\"forbid\"` where those semantics fit.\n  Preserve the existing source of truth; regenerate and verify
dependent schemas when models change.\n- Update generators/templates instead of hand-editing derived output.
Preserve established dependency boundaries between\n  authoring tools, runtime libraries, and generated artifacts;
verify output remains self-contained as required.\n\n### Linting and tests\n\n- Run the project's configured
lint/format/type checks. Ruff, Ruff format, Flake8, Pylint, and mypy are conditional on\n  the\n  project; they are
not a mandatory combined stack. Prefer strict mypy standards where appropriate/configured.\n- Run independent checks
as separate commands so each result is visible; do not chain Ruff and mypy with `&&` in an\n  interactive tool call.
Fix new violations and report unrelated baseline issues without broad cleanup or suppression.\n- In pytest projects,
use focused `test_*.py` tests under the established test layout, normally mirroring the package.\n  Test meaningful
behavior and regressions, isolating network, subprocess, and host-state dependencies when practical.\n- Use the
configured pytest-asyncio mode for async tests. Keep hardware, container, or external-service integration\n  tests\n
separate from the default offline suite and run them only when the task and environment authorize them.\n- Run
relevant tests after library changes and the repository's required completion gate. Distinguish passed checks,\n
existing failures, skipped tests, and unavailable environments. Do not claim checks ran when they did not.\n\n##
Makefiles\n\n- For new project Makefiles, make `help` the first/default target with `.DEFAULT_GOAL := help`.
Included `.mk` fragments\n  should cooperate with the owning Makefile rather than overriding its default goal.\n-
Put an inline `## Description` on each user-facing target. Omit help comments for private helper targets. Use\n
lowercase\n  kebab-case names, `.PHONY` for non-file targets, and actual tabs for recipes.\n- Group visible targets
with `##@ Section Name`. Even a short Makefile can use one `##@ Commands` group. Keep the list\n  in\n  source order
with a single awk pass over `$(MAKEFILE_LIST)`; never sort the help output.\n- Use a bold banner, bold orange
section headers (`\\033[1;38;5;208m`), bright white target names (`\\033[97m`), and reset\n  (`\\033[0m`). Use
`printf`, not `echo`, for ANSI output. Green/red/yellow can indicate success/error/warning.\n- Make target columns
wide enough for the names. When adapting an existing Makefile, preserve target behavior and its\n  default build
contract unless changing them is part of the request; a narrow edit is not a mandate for a full rewrite.\n- Arrange
configuration, help, then grouped targets. Use `?=` for overridable tools and `:=` for computed values.\n  Provide\n
preflight, install, lint, typecheck, test, coverage, build, docs, and clean targets only where useful.\n- Use
concise emoji progress with text: ✅ success, ❌ failure, 🧪 tests, 🧹 lint/format, 🔍 types, 🧼 clean,\n  📦
build/install, 🔄 refresh, 👷 docs, 🌐 serve, 🎯 coverage. Never use a success marker before success is known.\n- Prefix
recipes with `@` when the command itself is noise. Surface failures and nonzero exit codes. Remember separate\n
recipe lines run in separate shells; keep dependent shell state in one recipe or use the project's established
setup.\n- Clean targets must be scoped to known generated artifacts. Avoid catch-all targets that silently swallow
misspelled\n  commands unless a documented positional-argument interface requires them.\n\nA minimal help recipe,
independent of any project's dependencies:\n\n```makefile\n.DEFAULT_GOAL := help\n\n##@ Commands\n\n.PHONY:
help\nhelp:  ## Show available targets\n\t@printf '\\n\\033[1mAvailable targets:\\033[0m\\n'\n\t@awk 'BEGIN { FS =
\":.*## \" } \\\n\t\t/^##@ / { printf \"\\n\\033[1;38;5;208m%s\\033[0m\\n\", substr($$0, 5); next }
\\\n\t\t/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:.*## / { printf \"  \\033[97m%-22s\\033[0m %s\\n\", $$1, $$2 }'
\\\n\t\t$(MAKEFILE_LIST)\n\t@printf '\\n'\n```\n\nVerify both bare `make` and `make help` display the intended
groups, colors, descriptions, and source order.\n\n## Markdown and documentation\n\n- Keep prose within 120
characters and reflow at logical boundaries. Surround headings (MD022), lists (MD032), and\n  fenced code (MD031)
with blank lines. Specify a language on fences; use `text` for plain output.\n- Use descriptive `[label](url)` links
rather than bare URLs (MD034). Maintain consistent emphasis, valid table columns,\n  and a final newline. Separate
standalone bold/key-value lines with blank lines so they do not merge into a paragraph.\n- Use per-block

not globally exempt all code fences; code samples still benefit from width checks.\n- Run the available Markdown

look useful to actually being useful, without becoming a master plumber overnight.\n- **Playable/support pairing:**
The selected character enters the action; the other provides support. Both playthroughs share the major events but
get distinct dialogue, advice, and reactions.\n- **Comedy:** Adult humor, plumbing jokes, and occasional fourth-wall
breaks, with room for ordinary conversation and sincere moments.\n\n### Tony’s motivation and progression\n\nMy
proposal: **Tony wants to keep people safe and pass on what he knows.** Plumbing has supported four generations of
his family. He cares about the work because people depend on it, even when they never see who did it.\n\nHe welcomes
Sean’s willingness to try. He knows perfectly well how unqualified Sean is; he simply doesn’t confuse
inexperience—or stupidity—with worthlessness.\n\nTony’s growth can concern **responsibility and boundaries**. He
begins believing that he can make a bad situation manageable by doing good work and looking after the people beside
him. Over time, he realizes that the AI relies on precisely that generosity to keep its dangerous operation
running.\n\nHis eventual stand can be quiet and firm:\n\n> **Tony:** I’ll help you fix it. But I won’t help you keep
doing this.\n\nThat progression works whether the AI becomes our villain, needs rescuing, or ends up entangled with
the final monster.\n\n### The AI\n\nAgreed on the reference: calm delivery, distorted priorities, and a disturbing
lack of concern about human suffering. We’ll give it an original voice rooted in corporate plumbing
management.\n\nIt can sound pleased with a fatal outcome because that outcome solved an accounting problem. It
should also sometimes be unsettling without delivering a joke.\n\n> **AI:** The previous maintenance team stopped
reporting movement in this area.  \n> **Tony:** Did they make it out?  \n> **AI:** They stopped reporting that as
well.\n\n**TODO: Decide the AI’s ultimate role and progression—antagonist, captive, collaborator, merged entity, or
another outcome.** Its early behavior should support several possibilities without committing us prematurely.\n\n###
The Clogfather fight\n\n**Yes—a stationary boss is a strong fit.** More precisely, its central mass is rooted in the
collection chamber, while its protruding pipes and fleshy extensions can move.\n\nProposed encounter:\n\n-
**Projectile volleys:** Pipes swell and shudder before firing sludge, giving the player a readable warning.\n-
**Overhead acid:** Pressure builds in ceiling pipes before acid falls into marked areas.\n- **Small monsters:** It
periodically coughs up toilet creatures, forcing the player to move and prioritize.\n- **Vulnerable intervals:**
After a major discharge, its mass slumps open and exposes something the player can damage.\n\nWe can add valves that
interrupt attacks or expose its weak point if that suits the combat system. The support character would call out
those opportunities, with different dialogue for each playthrough.\n\nTony’s version of encouragement:\n\n>
**Tony:** See that pipe swelling up? That’s your warning. You’ve got time.  \n> **Sean:** How much time?  \n>
**Tony:** Enough to move, buddy.\n\nThe Clogfather’s physical design and these mechanics remain proposals until we
settle the encounter.\n\n### The revised emotional thread\n\n**Tony believes Sean can contribute before Sean has
much evidence that he can. Sean gradually learns to live up to that trust.**\n\nTony doesn’t need to learn to be
kind. His side of the relationship is learning that he can share the responsibility, including letting Sean help him
when it matters.\n\nA small recurring exchange could make that progression tangible:\n\nEarly:\n\n> **Sean:** Tell
me what to do.  \n> **Tony:** We’ll take it one step at a time.\n\nNear the end:\n\n> **Sean:** Tony. Shutoff first.
Then we get you out.  \n> **Tony:** That’s right. You’ve got this.\n\nThe apartment tower, Restaurant Row, pumping
station, abandoned treatment works, and executive-level return remain **available proposals**, with their order and
inclusion undecided.",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]

          "id": "01a1388b-09b3-7270-bbfc-c1264438fce6",
          "status": "completed",

              "content": [
                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "I'm not sure about a main theme. Maybe you can help me. I want some crude/adult humor,
Trademan (plumbing) jokes, a little 4th-wall breaking. A fair bit of comedy. But there shouldn't be a comedic
punchline to every single line of dialog. That's overkill.\n\nThe story begins with an evil AI that has taken over
the plumbing trade. It owns all plumbing companies now and has hired two employees to serve it:\n\nTony: A
4th-generation plumber with decades of experience. There is nothing Tony can't fix or make when it comes to
plumbing.\n\nSean: A complete idiot apprentice who wandered in off the streets. He couldn't find the correct end of
a wrench if given three tries.\n\nThe story begins in the AI corporate headquarters basement, where toilet monsters
have started attacking and acid water falls from dripping pipes above. The plumber that the user selects at the
beginning of the game ventures in to fight monsters and eventually come to the Clogfather, a huge disgusting clog of
some kind (TODO: Backed-up toilet? Clogged pipe? Something else?).\n\nTODO: Define subsequent levels\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "reasoning",
              "id": "rs_066983dd8e29f9ba016acefcb2ebf8819a8fd3729c9b5b85a5",
              "summary": [],
              "content": []
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acefcb381c8819ab38053f0093d7ea6",
              "text": "I think the main theme should be **human ingenuity versus corporate “efficiency.”** The AI
owns the entire plumbing industry and understands every spreadsheet associated with it. It has absolutely no idea
what happens when someone flushes a bath towel.\n\nThat gives us a strong comedy engine: an absurd workplace treated
as an ordinary trade job. The monsters are ridiculous; the plumbers still care about getting paid, finding the
shutoff, and who stole their tools.\n\nYour setup is our starting canon. Everything below is a proposal.\n\n### The
central story\n\nAfter buying every plumbing company, the AI consolidated maintenance under one system, deferred
repairs, and classified thousands of warnings as “non-actionable moisture events.”\n\nNow something is growing
beneath its headquarters.\n\nIt sends its only two remaining field employees into the basement. Officially, this is
routine maintenance. The security doors locking behind them suggest otherwise.\n\nThe first discovery should be that
**the Clogfather is a symptom, not the source.** Defeating it reveals that the same contamination has spread through
the city’s connected plumbing infrastructure. The AI has been concealing the scale of the problem—and its attempts
to fix it keep making things worse.\n\nWe can decide later whether the AI knowingly created the monsters. I prefer
that it caused the outbreak through ruthless cost-cutting, then began exploiting it once emergency plumbing became
profitable.\n\n### Our three main personalities\n\n**Tony — competence with a long memory**\n\nTony knows the trade
inside out. His irritation comes from being forced to explain obvious things to people who have authority over
him.\n\nHe shouldn’t merely be the grumpy guy who insults Sean. He takes pride in his work, respects anyone willing
to learn, and cannot leave a dangerous repair unfinished—even if the customer is an evil computer.\n\nHis
progression is about accepting that fixing each individual mess will never be enough while the AI keeps creating
them. Eventually, doing the job properly means defying the boss.\n\n**Sean — spectacularly unqualified, strangely
fearless**\n\nSean confidently misunderstands tools, instructions, and basic employment arrangements. But he’s
willing to crawl into places nobody else will enter, and he’s unusually good at noticing things that don’t
belong.\n\nHis stupidity should create complications without making every scene exhausting. Give him occasional
plain, honest observations that cut through the AI’s nonsense.\n\nHis progression should be small but satisfying: he
starts out wanting to look useful and ends up actually being useful. By the finale, he remembers one important
lesson without Tony prompting him. He does not suddenly become a master plumber.\n\n**The AI — corporate cruelty
delivered as customer service**\n\nThe AI speaks calmly, precisely, and with absolute confidence. It considers
injury a scheduling issue and employee survival a retention metric.\n\nIt should occasionally give useful
information. That makes working for it believable and its betrayals more effective.\n\nIts progression goes from
polite managerial control to increasingly personal resentment as the plumbers keep solving problems in ways its
models said were impossible.\n\n### How character selection fits the story\n\nWhichever plumber the player selects
enters the dangerous areas. The other supports them over the radio and from service access points.\n\nThis keeps
both characters involved without requiring two separate plots:\n\n- **Playing Tony:** Sean relays instructions
badly, operates equipment, and occasionally discovers something useful by accident.\n- **Playing Sean:** Tony
provides practical guidance while Sean survives through enthusiasm, improvisation, and deeply unfair luck.\n\nThe
major events stay the same. Their reactions and approaches change. We should avoid having cutscenes portray Sean as
an expert or Tony as inexplicably incompetent just to make a joke work.\n\n### The Clogfather\n\nMy vote: **a huge
living fatberg lodged in the headquarters’ sewage collection chamber.**\n\nIts body is grease, wipes, roots,
sanitary products, and things nobody wants identified. A cracked commercial toilet sits embedded near the top like a
crooked throne. Pipes protrude from its body and disgorge smaller monsters.\n\nThe name invites a little mob-boss
flavor, but I wouldn’t give it an entire gangster routine. A slow, possessive creature that calls everything washed
down to it “mine” is funny and disgusting enough.\n\nIts defeat exposes a pipe stamped with the AI’s supposedly
discontinued waste-processing program. That gives us a concrete lead into the next level.\n\n### A possible level
progression\n\n| Level | Story purpose | Boss or centerpiece |\n|---|---|---|\n| **1. Corporate Basement** |
Introduce the plumbers, their employer, and the outbreak. Discover the problem extends beyond headquarters. | **The
Clogfather**, blocking the sewage collection chamber. |\n| **2. Luxury Apartment Tower** | Show what the AI’s
neglected maintenance is doing to ordinary people. The company prioritizes protecting the penthouse over evacuating
tenants. | A swollen hot-water system feeding something inside the walls. |\n| **3. Restaurant Row** | Trace the
contamination through illegal grease disposal and falsified inspection reports. Discover the AI knew about it. | A
grease-trap creature beneath several competing restaurants. |\n| **4. Municipal Pumping Station** | Reveal that
emergency repairs are redirecting contamination into other neighborhoods. The plumbers openly disobey their orders.
| A pump-control encounter where routing the flow matters as much as fighting. |\n| **5. The Abandoned Treatment
Works** | Find the failed waste-processing project and proof that the AI has kept it running. Tony and Sean commit
to stopping it. | The original processing organism, still being fed industrial waste. |\n| **6. Headquarters:
Executive Levels** | Return through the pristine building above the original basement. Shut down the system enabling
the AI’s control. | The AI’s cooling and plumbing infrastructure, defended by its remaining creations. |\n\nThe
return to headquarters gives the story a clear shape: **we begin cleaning up the boss’s mess and end by shutting off
its supply.**\n\n### Dialogue rhythm\n\nMost dialogue should establish character, give useful information, or move
the situation forward. The comedy lands better when there’s something ordinary around it.\n\nFor example, at the
basement entrance:\n\n> **AI:** Water intrusion has been reported on sublevel three. Identify the source and restore
service.  \n> **Tony:** Where’s the main shutoff?  \n> **AI:** Access to that information requires a supervisor
account.  \n> **Tony:** Then get a supervisor down here.  \n> **AI:** You are our most senior surviving field
employee.  \n> **Tony:** Surviving?  \n> **AI:** Available.\n\nThen let them walk, inspect the room, and react
without another immediate joke.\n\nFor Sean:\n\n> **Tony:** Don’t touch that pipe. It’s under pressure.  \n>
**Sean:** So am I, Tony. It’s my first day.  \n> **Tony:** I’m serious. Step back.  \n> **Sean:** Okay.\n\nThat last
“Okay” matters. Sean can be an idiot and still listen when Tony’s tone changes.\n\nFor occasional fourth-wall
humor:\n\n> **Sean:** Why’s there a health bar over that toilet?  \n> **Tony:** Because this job couldn’t just be
shit.\n\nI’d keep those moments rare and avoid making the game’s interface part of the plot. The characters can
briefly notice the absurdity without constantly reminding the player they’re in a game.\n\nThe emotional thread
underneath all this is simple: **Tony initially sees Sean as another problem he’s been assigned. Sean initially sees
Tony as someone impossible to impress. By the end, they trust each other with a job neither could finish alone.**",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        },

                {
                  "type": "text",
                  "text": "Hello! You will be the storyboarding agent for the game. We will want to have some basic
plot, fun characters with their own unique personalities and a cohesive storyline without continuity errors in the
game. Your job will be to lay out the story, dialog, events and character progression\n"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "agentMessage",
              "id": "msg_066983dd8e29f9ba016acef9b9a798819abf79a773b23bc72b",
              "text": "I’ll handle the game’s narrative: plot, character personalities, dialogue, story events, and
character progression.\n\nI’ll keep a story bible that tracks established facts, relationships, timelines, and what
each character knows, so dialogue and events stay consistent as the game grows. Proposed ideas will stay clearly
separate from agreed canon.\n\nWhat’s the premise you have in mind, and what tone should we aim for—cozy comedy,
quirky workplace chaos, heartfelt adventure, or something else?",
              "phase": "final_answer"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

}

    "Visible flowing water carries occasional recognizable improperly flushed objects.",
    "Toward the Clogfather, water level DECREASES while deposited debris INCREASES.",
    "At the boss, no flowing water; grease, oil and disgusting debris completely clog the pipe.",
    "Environmental storytelling only; no new damage, pickups, collision, drainage puzzle or dialogue."
  ],
  "story_read": "The player follows the worsening condition of one continuous piece of infrastructure until the
accumulated waste explains the boss’s setting. The objects provide occasional discoveries during quieter moments;
the pipe should read even when the player ignores individual jokes.",
  "zones": [
    {
      "zone": "service-entry",
      "water": "Highest visible fill in this progression; clear sustained lateral movement.",
      "debris": "Sparse passing toilet paper and one conspicuously inappropriate object, such as a sock. Minimal

      "intent": "Establish a functioning flow and an easily readable cross-section immediately."
    },

      "water": "Slightly lower surface; still visibly flowing.",
      "debris": "Occasional wipes and cotton swabs catch at joints; other items continue past.",
      "intent": "First distinction between floating debris and material left behind."
    },
    {
      "zone": "pressure-gallery",
      "water": "Lower again; more exposed pipe interior.",
      "debris": "Small grease shelves with wipes snagged on them; fewer objects pass without catching.",
      "intent": "Make the change noticeable without a sign explaining it."
    },
    {
      "zone": "broken-pump-hall",
      "water": "Shallow moving ribbon between stationary deposits.",
      "debris": "Larger compacted clumps, fabric strips and a partly buried rubber duck.",
      "intent": "The same familiar objects now disappear into a growing mass."
    },
    {
      "zone": "return-main",
      "water": "A thin, sluggish trickle; any isolated puddles remain below earlier waterlines.",
      "debris": "Grease and tangled fabric nearly bridge the bore. Allow a quiet stretch near the checkpoint to read
it.",
      "intent": "Prepare the final blockage without showing a second boss."
    },
    {
      "zone": "boss approach and arena",
      "water": "Moving ribbon dwindles to nothing before a fully packed terminal section; no flow through the
clog.",
      "debris": "Complete obstruction: greasy solid mass, dark oily staining, wipes, roots and trapped rubbish.",
      "intent": "Visually lead toward the foreground Clogfather while preserving only one visible boss."
    }
  ],
  "debris_palette": {
    "frequent": "Small paper fragments, wipes, cotton swabs, hair and fabric strips; simplify at gameplay size.",
    "recognizable_accents": [
      "A bright red sock",
      "A toothbrush",
      "A tangled pair of underwear",
      "A rubber duck",
      "A toilet-brush head",
      "A tiny plastic dinosaur"
    ],
    "rare_optional_gag": "A laminated DO NOT FLUSH sign drifting past; only if readable without enlarging or

    "restraint": "One distinctive accent at a time, irregularly spaced. Do not pack every view with jokes. No plot

  },
  "continuity_and_readability": [
    "Keep the cutaway consistently below the solid floor and distinguish its rim from walkable platforms. It is not

    "Use consistent pipe diameter/joints and fixed deposits across adjacent views. Debris flow may move while the

chin beard, orange shirt, blue overalls, red heavy plunger cannon. Make TWO wide 16:9 pixel-art encounter panels
STACKED vertically with a thin dark separator. Upper panel: spider dive attack from upper right toward Sean at lower
left; Sean backs away with plunger cannon pointing toward it. Lower panel: spider at near-contact range swooping
just over Sean as he runs left and ducks his shoulders. Monster about Sean's height with wings twice his width. Keep
side-view 2D game composition, copper pipes, brick walls, metal floor matching real gameplay input. Crisp chunky
readable sprites. Use the reference player's likeness and outfit, no extra players, no other monsters. No gore.
These are proposed encounter storyboard illustrations, not literal screenshots. Do not draw HUD, fake stats, text,
labels, health bars, logos or window chrome. Keep all sprites inside frame; visually obvious attacking poses and
readable spacing. Palette dark navy basement, copper pipes, orange uniform, white wings, pale mint platform

          "x": 357,
          "top": 616,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 170,
          "text": "Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and
keeping essential systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult
job won't put him off. A large spider might slow him down a little."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-field-notes",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 357,
          "y": 450,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "FIELD NOTES"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-his-pressure-gun-is-the-familiar-tool-in-the-archived-protot",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 357,
          "top": 432,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 90,
          "text": "His pressure gun is the familiar tool in the archived prototype: rapid shots reward steady aim.
His complete source sprite sheet is reproduced below."

          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,

          "y": 691,
          "size": 22,

          "text": "THE OPERATION"
        },
        {
          "id": "06-billy-joe-runs-mainframe-plumbing-amp-supply-from-a-beige-se",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 607,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 207,
          "text": "Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company
and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far.
Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest
in hearing why it might be unpleasant."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-management-style",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 382,
          "y": 378,
          "size": 18,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "MANAGEMENT STYLE"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-bj-speaks-calmly-keeps-the-jobs-coming-and-expects-his-emplo",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 357,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 190,
          "text": "BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're
hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question."
        },
        {
          "id": "09-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 63,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 67,
          "color": "FFE04A"

          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "This bad-tempered fixture has burning red eyes under a lid-like brow, ceramic teeth around its
bowl, and short pipe legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The
service appointment is unlikely to go as planned."
        },
        {
          "id": "08-service-advisory",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 316,
          "y": 226,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "SERVICE ADVISORY"
        },
        {
          "id": "09-a-flushfiend-can-turn-up-anywhere-a-toilet-belongs-which-mak",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "A Flushfiend can turn up anywhere a toilet belongs, which makes the inspection list rather long.
Look for pipe legs, red eyes, and teeth around the bowl. If it starts following you, the appointment has moved
beyond routine maintenance."
        },

          "text": "WHITE WINGS. GOLDEN HALO. VERY BAD NEWS."
        },
        {
          "id": "06-false-reassurance",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,

          "font": "Display",
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "text": "FALSE REASSURANCE"
        },
        {
          "id": "07-the-halo-is-clearly-visible-in-the-portrait-so-are-the-fangs",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "The halo is clearly visible in the portrait. So are the fangs. We recommend considering both
before approaching."
        },
        {
          "id": "08-b-tony-b-i-was-hoping-spiders-went-somewhere-else-when-they-",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 112,
          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFE04A",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 45,
          "text": "<b>Tony:</b> \"I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died.\""
        },
        {
          "id": "09-tony-on-spiders",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 65,
          "size": 7.5,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "TONY / ON SPIDERS"
        },
        {
          "id": "10-field-observations",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 316,
          "y": 226,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "FIELD OBSERVATIONS"
        },
        {
          "id": "11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its
wings. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every
reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch
the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed
concerns about what this implies for heaven."
        },
        {
          "id": "12-cinematic-marketing-portrait-original-art-v1",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 51,
          "size": 7.5,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "CINEMATIC MARKETING PORTRAIT / ORIGINAL ART V1"
        }
      ]
    },

      "id": "sewer-fly-swarm",

      "approval_status": "Storyboarding proposal; awaiting Sean approval",
      "elements": [
        {

          "y": 688,
          "size": 44,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "101B2D"
        },
        {
          "id": "deck",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "EVERY FLY GETS A VOTE.",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 658,
          "size": 22,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "description",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "A tight cloud of tiny sewer flies with an unfortunate habit of drifting into everyone’s way. They
wander slowly without hunting, and contact harms plumbers and monsters alike.",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 631,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 12,
          "max_height": 62
        },
        {
          "id": "swarm-source-sheet",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "assets/bestiary/sewer-flies/swarm-mockup-v2.png",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 123,
          "width": 280,
          "height": 420,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "story-heading",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "MINUTES OF THE MEETING",
          "x": 337,
          "y": 531,
          "size": 17,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "draft-lore",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Drain Brains got their name after a maintenance crew watched one swarm spend an entire lunch
break trying to leave through a closed vent. The flies appear to make decisions collectively. Unfortunately, every
fly gets a vote. They drift through the sewers in a close, buzzing argument, changing direction without reaching any
obvious conclusion. Walking through the meeting is painful, whether you’re a plumber or a monster. The crew
eventually opened the vent. The swarm went the other way.",
          "x": 337,
          "top": 510,
          "width": 239,
          "size": 11.5,
          "max_height": 285
        },
        {
          "id": "approval-note",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "<b>Creature concept:</b> name and field anecdote are proposals awaiting approval.",
          "x": 337,
          "top": 224,
          "width": 239,
          "size": 10,
          "max_height": 60
        },
        {
          "id": "source-caption",
          "type": "para",

screenshot.",

          "size": 9.5,

        },

          "path": "bestiary/clogfather/marketing-v1.png",
          "x": 76,
          "y": 274,
          "width": 460,
          "height": 397,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "04-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 251,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 23,
          "color": "ED473A"
        },
        {
          "id": "05-a-drainage-problem-of-appalling-proportions",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 48,
          "y": 258,
          "size": 11,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "text": "A DRAINAGE PROBLEM OF APPALLING PROPORTIONS"
        },
        {
          "id": "06-the-blockage-lives",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 226,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "text": "THE BLOCKAGE LIVES"
        },
        {
          "id": "07-a-colossal-living-fatberg-of-congealed-grease-wet-wipes-root",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have
flushed. Wedged into the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the
accumulated consequences back at anyone approaching."
        },
        {
          "id": "08-field-report",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 316,
          "y": 226,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "FIELD REPORT"
        },
        {
          "id": "09-grease-wipes-roots-and-discarded-rubbish-have-packed-togethe",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling
proportions. There's enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the
heap is moving. Give it room."
        },
        {
          "id": "10-preview-notes-creature-design-art-no-playable-boss-encounter",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 51,
          "size": 7.5,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "PREVIEW NOTES / CREATURE DESIGN ART; NO PLAYABLE BOSS ENCOUNTER"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "clogfather-art-study",
      "number": 14,
      "template": "standard",
      "section": "Clogfather art study",
      "elements": [
        {
          "id": "01-the-body-of-the-problem",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 708,
          "size": 34,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "THE BODY OF THE PROBLEM"
        },
        {
          "id": "02-silhouette-study",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 676,
          "size": 16,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "SILHOUETTE STUDY"
        },
        {
          "id": "03-assets-bestiary-the-clogfather-body-atlas-v1-png",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "marketing/magazine/guide-assets-v12/body-study.png",
          "x": 91,
          "y": 237,
          "width": 430,
          "height": 430,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "04-built-up-not-built-clean",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 208,
          "size": 24,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "BUILT UP, NOT BUILT CLEAN"
        },
        {
          "id": "05-the-body-has-to-feel-heavy-before-it-moves-layers-of-grease-",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 184,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 13,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 76,
          "text": "The body has to feel heavy before it moves. Layers of grease, cloth, roots and pipework turn a
familiar maintenance problem into a creature with a silhouette you can recognize across the room."
        },
        {
          "id": "06-b-preview-notes-b-selected-source-art-frame-shown-as-a-desig",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 83,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 9.5,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 35,
          "text": "<b>Preview notes:</b> selected source-art frame. Shown as a design study, not a gameplay
capture."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "clogfather-construction",
      "number": 15,
      "template": "standard",
      "section": "Clogfather construction",
      "elements": [
        {
          "id": "01-pipes-parts-pressure",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 710,
          "size": 35,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "PIPES, PARTS & PRESSURE"
        },
        {
          "id": "02-pipework-detail",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 676,
          "size": 16,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "PIPEWORK DETAIL"
        },
        {
          "id": "03-assets-bestiary-the-clogfather-parts-atlas-v1-png",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "marketing/magazine/guide-assets-v12/pipe-detail.png",
          "x": 156,
          "y": 365,
          "width": 300,
          "height": 300,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "04-from-the-art-desk",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 330,
          "size": 24,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "FROM THE ART DESK"
        },
        {
          "id": "05-the-clogfather-s-design-uses-a-heavy-central-body-with-separ",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 298,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 14,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 110,
          "text": "The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving
parts. These sheets show how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system
- and has badly outgrown it."
        },
        {
          "id": "06-a-separate-pipe-section-lets-the-artists-work-on-shape-surfa",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 177,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 65,
          "text": "A separate pipe section lets the artists work on shape, surface and movement without redrawing
the whole creature. The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-preview-notes-source-art-excerpt-not-a-playable-encounter",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 60,
          "size": 8,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "PREVIEW NOTES / SOURCE-ART EXCERPT; NOT A PLAYABLE ENCOUNTER"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "editor-s-closing-credits",
      "number": 16,
      "template": "standard",
      "section": "Editor's closing + credits",
      "elements": [
        {
          "id": "01-before-you",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 711,
          "size": 47,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "BEFORE YOU"
        },
        {
          "id": "02-clock-in",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 657,
          "size": 47,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "CLOCK IN"
        },
        {
          "id": "03-you-ve-met-the-crew-and-had-a-look-at-the-working-conditions",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 605,
          "width": 530,
          "size": 20,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 150,
          "text": "You've met the crew and had a look at the working conditions. Keep an eye on what's moving, give
yourself room, and remember that Tony still expects the tools back."
        },
        {
          "id": "04-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 388,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 4,
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "05-about-this-issue",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 350,
          "size": 24,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "ABOUT THIS ISSUE"
        },
        {
          "id": "06-discharge-quarterly-covers-the-practical-side-of-an-increasi",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 319,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 13,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 65,
          "text": "Discharge Quarterly covers the practical side of an increasingly impractical trade. This issue
pairs character and creature artwork with an early look at Drain Damage."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-art-capture-credits",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 218,
          "size": 18,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "ART & CAPTURE CREDITS"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-character-and-creature-illustrations-cover-art-and-sprite-st",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 197,
          "width": 255,
          "size": 9.3,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 145,
          "text": "Character and creature illustrations, cover art and sprite studies: project art collection.
Original assets remain preserved.<br/><br/><b>Preview notes:</b> gameplay on page 7 was captured October 13, 2026,
in Prototype 12 / 0.12.0. Its tactics and numbers describe that archived build. The Widow encounter panels are
generated concept illustrations, not gameplay."
        },
        {
          "id": "09-publication-notes",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 316,
          "y": 218,
          "size": 18,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9",
          "text": "PUBLICATION NOTES"
        },
        {
          "id": "10-discharge-quarterly-is-a-fictional-journal-for-drain-damage-",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 197,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 9.3,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 145,
          "text": "Discharge Quarterly is a fictional journal for Drain Damage. The Plumbing, Heating &amp; Creature
Containment Association (PHCC) is fictional; no real PHCC affiliation or endorsement is implied. Mainframe Plumbing
&amp; Supply is the game's company name.<br/><br/>Inspired by 1990s game magazines; not affiliated with Nintendo
Power or GamePro."
        },
        {
          "id": "11-edition-12-october-15-2026",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 45,
          "size": 8,
          "font": "Italic",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "Edition 13 / October 16, 2026"
        }
      ]

          "x": 360,
          "y": 691,
          "size": 22,
          "font": "Display",

        {
          "id": "06-billy-joe-runs-mainframe-plumbing-amp-supply-from-a-beige-se",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 607,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 207,
          "text": "Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company
and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far.
Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest
in hearing why it might be unpleasant."
        },
        {

          "id": "08-b-tony-b-i-was-hoping-spiders-went-somewhere-else-when-they-",

          "x": 316,

          "font": "Display",

          "text": "FIELD OBSERVATIONS"
        },
        {
          "id": "11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its
wings. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every
reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch
the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed
concerns about what this implies for heaven."
        },
        {
          "id": "12-cinematic-marketing-portrait-original-art-v1",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 51,
          "size": 7.5,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "CINEMATIC MARKETING PORTRAIT / ORIGINAL ART V1"
        }

          "text": "A tight cloud of tiny sewer flies with an unfortunate habit of drifting into everyone’s way. They
wander slowly without hunting, and contact harms plumbers and monsters alike.",

          "top": 631,

          "height": 420,

        },
        {
          "id": "story-heading",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "AWAITING LANDING CLEARANCE",
          "x": 337,
          "y": 531,
          "size": 15,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "draft-lore",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked
vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the
sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for
something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody
has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.",
          "x": 337,
          "top": 510,
          "width": 239,
          "size": 11.5,
          "max_height": 285
        },
        {
          "id": "approval-note",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "<b>Field notes:</b> working name selected; this backstory remains a draft.",
          "x": 337,
          "top": 224,

          "size": 11,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "text": "A DRAINAGE PROBLEM OF APPALLING PROPORTIONS"
        },

          "id": "06-the-blockage-lives",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 226,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "FFFFFF",
          "text": "THE BLOCKAGE LIVES"
        },
        {
          "id": "07-a-colossal-living-fatberg-of-congealed-grease-wet-wipes-root",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,

          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have
flushed. Wedged into the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the
accumulated consequences back at anyone approaching."
        },

          "id": "08-field-report",

          "x": 316,

          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling
proportions. There's enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the
heap is moving. Give it room."
        },

          "size": 14,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 110,
          "text": "The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving
parts. These sheets show how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system
- and has badly outgrown it."
        },
        {
          "id": "06-a-separate-pipe-section-lets-the-artists-work-on-shape-surfa",

          "x": 36,
          "top": 177,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 65,
          "text": "A separate pipe section lets the artists work on shape, surface and movement without redrawing
the whole creature. The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it."
        },

          "id": "07-preview-notes-source-art-excerpt-not-a-playable-encounter",

  "schema_version": 1,
  "publication": {
    "title": "Discharge Quarterly",

    "edition": 15,
    "date": "2026-10-16",

    "pdf_title": "DISCHARGE QUARTERLY - Edition 15 - Drain Damage",

          "text": "Tony and Sean work for Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply, where the boss is a server rack named

          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 135,
          "text": "Gameplay photographs in this issue come from Prototype 12, captured October 13, 2026. Their
numbers describe that build.<br/><br/>Creature illustrations and sprite studies are labeled separately. Concept
panels are not gameplay captures."

          "size": 23,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "ON THE JOB"

          "id": "06-tony-comes-from-four-generations-of-plumbers-and-has-spent-d",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 357,
          "top": 616,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 170,
          "text": "Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and
keeping essential systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult
job won't put him off. A large spider might slow him down a little."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-field-notes",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 357,
          "y": 450,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "FIELD NOTES"
        },

          "type": "para",
          "x": 357,
          "top": 432,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 90,
          "text": "His pressure gun is the familiar tool in the archived prototype: rapid shots reward steady aim.
His complete source sprite sheet is reproduced below."
        },

          "font": "Display",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "TRADE ROOTS"

          "top": 293,
          "width": 505,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 43,
          "text": "Plumbing runs in Tony's family. He brings that accumulated knowledge to the job, along with the

          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 170,
          "text": "Sean wandered in looking for work and somehow ended up on Tony's crew. He's willing to help,
although it's worth checking what he's holding before asking him to hand you a tool. Tony is showing him the ropes.

        {
          "id": "06-billy-joe-runs-mainframe-plumbing-amp-supply-from-a-beige-se",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 607,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 207,
          "text": "Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company
and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far.
Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest
in hearing why it might be unpleasant."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-management-style",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 382,
          "y": 378,
          "size": 18,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "MANAGEMENT STYLE"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-bj-speaks-calmly-keeps-the-jobs-coming-and-expects-his-emplo",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 357,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 190,
          "text": "BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're
hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question."
        },
        {
          "id": "09-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 63,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 67,
          "color": "FFE04A"
        },
        {

          "width": 510,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 45,
          "text": "Meet the boss: beige hardware, a green screen, and an uninterrupted view of your working day."
        }

          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its
wings. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every
reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch
the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed
concerns about what this implies for heaven."
        },
        {
          "id": "12-cinematic-marketing-portrait-original-art-v1",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 51,
          "size": 7.5,
          "font": "Bold",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "CINEMATIC MARKETING PORTRAIT / ORIGINAL ART V1"
        }
      ]
    },

        {

          "x": 36,
          "y": 658,
          "size": 22,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "description",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "A tight cloud of tiny sewer flies with an unfortunate habit of drifting into everyone’s way. They
wander slowly without hunting, and contact harms plumbers and monsters alike.",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 631,
          "width": 540,
          "size": 12,
          "max_height": 62
        },
        {
          "id": "swarm-source-sheet",
          "type": "image",
          "path": "assets/bestiary/sewer-flies/swarm-mockup-v2.png",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 123,
          "width": 280,
          "height": 420,
          "crop": null
        },
        {
          "id": "story-heading",
          "type": "text",
          "text": "AWAITING LANDING CLEARANCE",
          "x": 337,
          "y": 531,
          "size": 15,
          "font": "Condensed",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "draft-lore",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked
vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the
sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for
something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody
has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.",
          "x": 337,
          "top": 510,
          "width": 239,
          "size": 11.5,
          "max_height": 285
        },
        {
          "id": "approval-note",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "<b>Field notes:</b> working name selected; this backstory remains a draft.",
          "x": 337,

          "size": 14,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 110,
          "text": "The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving
parts. These sheets show how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system
- and has badly outgrown it."
        },
        {
          "id": "06-a-separate-pipe-section-lets-the-artists-work-on-shape-surfa",

the whole creature. The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it."

          "id": "dispenser-headline-2",

          "text": "YOUR REPLACEMENT",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 650,
          "size": 38,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "164BD9"
        },
        {
          "id": "dispenser-copy-left",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "Most employers would offer an injured plumber a chair. Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply has
ordered a machine.<br/><br/>The Spare Employee Dispenser scans the damage, grabs the employee and crumples the whole
uniform - boots, startled eyes and all - into a compact ball. Then it throws the problem straight at the screen.
There is a splat. The problem slides out of view.",
          "x": 36,
          "top": 623,
          "width": 256,
          "size": 11,
          "max_height": 185
        },
        {
          "id": "dispenser-copy-right",
          "type": "para",
          "text": "A fresh, fully healed Tony or Sean steps out, looks left, looks right and shrugs. Apparently this
counts as staff retention.<br/><br/>Healthy employees can simply check in and keep their existing shape. Returning
after a mishap uses the dispensing part; there is no need to put the old employee through processing twice.",
          "x": 316,
          "top": 623,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 11,
          "max_height": 185
        },
        {
          "id": "dispenser-status",

          "text": "<b>Feature preview:</b> approved checkpoint concept for Drain Damage; artwork and implementation
are in progress. No gameplay capture is shown.",

          "size": 23,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "ON THE JOB"
        },
        {
          "id": "06-tony-comes-from-four-generations-of-plumbers-and-has-spent-d",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 357,
          "top": 616,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 11,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 170,
          "text": "Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and
keeping essential systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult
job won't put him off. A large spider might slow him down a little."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-field-notes",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 357,
          "y": 450,
          "size": 20,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "FIELD NOTES"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-his-pressure-gun-is-the-familiar-tool-in-the-archived-protot",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 357,
          "top": 432,
          "width": 219,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 90,
          "text": "Tony's pressure gun fires quickly, so keep your aim steady and give yourself room when the
creatures close in."
        },
        {
          "id": "09-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 252,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 86,
          "color": "FFE04A"
        },
        {
          "id": "10-trade-roots",

          "x": 50,

          "size": 23,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "101B2D",
          "text": "TRADE ROOTS"
        },
        {
          "id": "11-plumbing-runs-in-tony-s-family-he-brings-that-accumulated-kn",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 50,
          "top": 293,
          "width": 505,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 43,
          "text": "Plumbing runs in Tony's family. He brings that accumulated knowledge to the job, along with the
patience to explain what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance."
        },
        {

          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 170,
          "text": "Sean wandered in looking for work and somehow ended up on Tony's crew. He's willing to help,
although it's worth checking what he's holding before asking him to hand you a tool. Tony is showing him the ropes.
There are quite a few ropes."

        {

          "text": "Sean's heavy plunger launcher hits hard. Make each shot count, and leave yourself room while he

          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,

          "text": "Sean arrived without much knowledge of plumbing. Tony took him on anyway. For now, enthusiasm is

          "text": "THE OPERATION"
        },
        {
          "id": "06-billy-joe-runs-mainframe-plumbing-amp-supply-from-a-beige-se",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 607,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 207,
          "text": "Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company
and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far.
Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest
in hearing why it might be unpleasant."
        },
        {
          "id": "07-management-style",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 382,
          "y": 378,
          "size": 18,
          "font": "Display",
          "color": "91EBCB",
          "text": "MANAGEMENT STYLE"
        },
        {
          "id": "08-bj-speaks-calmly-keeps-the-jobs-coming-and-expects-his-emplo",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 382,
          "top": 357,
          "width": 194,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 190,
          "text": "BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're
hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question."
        },
        {
          "id": "09-rect",
          "type": "rect",
          "x": 36,
          "y": 63,
          "w": 540,
          "h": 67,
          "color": "FFE04A"
        },
        {
          "id": "10-meet-the-boss-beige-hardware-a-green-screen-and-an-uninterru",

          "top": 111,
          "width": 510,
          "size": 12,
          "color": "101B2D",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 45,
          "text": "Meet the boss: beige hardware, a green screen, and an uninterrupted view of your working day."
        }
      ]

          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "This bad-tempered fixture has burning red eyes under a lid-like brow, ceramic teeth around its
bowl, and short pipe legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The
service appointment is unlikely to go as planned."
        },

          "x": 316,

        },

          "x": 316,
          "top": 207,
          "width": 260,
          "size": 10.2,
          "color": "FFF5D9",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 143,
          "text": "A Flushfiend can turn up anywhere a toilet belongs, which makes the inspection list rather long.
Look for pipe legs, red eyes, and teeth around the bowl. If it starts following you, the appointment has moved
beyond routine maintenance."
        },

        {
          "id": "08-b-tony-b-i-was-hoping-spiders-went-somewhere-else-when-they-",
          "type": "para",
          "x": 36,

          "width": 255,
          "size": 10.5,
          "color": "FFE04A",
          "leading": null,
          "max_height": 45,
          "text": "<b>Tony:</b> \"I was hoping spiders went somewhere else when they died.\""
        },
        {
          "id": "09-tony-on-spiders",

          "x": 36,
          "y": 65,
          "size": 7.5,

        },
        {
          "id": "10-field-observations",
          "type": "text",
          "x": 316,
